#1791. Wayne Rooney and Paddy McGuinness laud football super-agent Paul Stretford - who has worked with Man United icon since his teens - at star-studded Global Football Industry Awards

Published: 13:14 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 13:15 EST, 9 November 2026

Wayne Rooney has led the praise for football super-agent Paul Stretford as the industry heavyweight was honoured at the Global Football Industry Awards.

Stretford, alongside Kenneth Shepherd, received the prestigious Lifetime Achievement Award at this year's Awards in recognition of their longstanding careers and work on Soccer Aid for Unicef.

He has worked by Rooney's side for more than 20 years, and has recently appeared on the former footballer's reality TV show, which he fronts alongside wife Coleen.

Rooney presented Stretford with the award himself, alongside Toni Duggan and comedian Paddy McGuinness. Theo Walcott and Jamie Carragher hosted the ceremony.

Rooney said of his agent and close friend: 'Paul in particular has had a major influence on my life since I was a teenager and has guided my career.

'Both Paul and Kenneth are very deserving of this award. It is not before time and I'm delighted for both of them. The work they've done on Soccer Aid is phenomenal too.'

Wayne Rooney (centre) has lauded close friend and football super agent Paul Stretford (right)

Stretford doesn't just look after Rooney, having also worked with the likes of Harry Maguire since founding Proactive Sports Management, now known as Triple S Sports Group, in 1987.

Shepherd, meanwhile, has been instrumental in the success of the Soccer Aid initiative which has raised more than £137million for Unicef since it launched in 2006.

#1790. The Numbers Game: Spain and England to fight it out for top spot

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Top spot in Group A3 is on the line as Spain and England go head-to-head in the Nations League on Sunday.

Spain occupy top spot, having recorded a perfect campaign so far with five wins from five, following their 2-0 victory over 10-man Czechia on Thursday.

But England, who secured their qualification for the quarter-finals with their 2-1 win over Croatia last time out, are only three points behind La Roja.

The Three Lions lost their opener to Spain but have since won four straight games, and they are the top-scoring team in the competition, with 16 goals.

The world champions have an impeccable unbeaten streak to protect when they step out at the Metropolitano, while England will be determined to prove they can go toe-to-toe with the best.

So, who is expected to come out on top in this pivotal clash? Using Opta data, we look at the key storylines ahead of the clash in Madrid.

Given their 100% record so far, it is perhaps no surprise that Spain are quite heavy favourites to claim three points this weekend.

Across the Opta supercomputer's 10,000 pre-match simulations, Spain were triumphant in 59.6%, with England's win probability sitting at 19.3%.

Back in Madrid! #VamosEspaña | #NationsLeague https://t.co/RrbujvJpPn

— Spanish Football (@SpainIsFootball) November 13, 2026

Spain have won seven of their last 10 matches against England (D1 L2), including the most recent two: 2-1 in the Euro 2024 final and 3-2 in the Nations League at Wembley in September.

This is England's first away game against Spain since a 3-2 win back in October 2018, also in the Nations League.

They have won their only other competitive away game against La Roja, beating them 2-1 in a European Championship qualifier in May 1968, but Thomas Tuchel's side will have to overturn the odds to keep that run going.

There is no shying away from the fact that Spain are currently the team to beat in world football, and they have looked unstoppable.

They are on a record 43-game unbeaten streak in all competitions (excluding penalty shoot-outs), with their last defeat a 1-0 friendly loss to Colombia in March 2024.

Not only that, but they have won each of their last 12 games in all competitions since drawing 0-0 with Cape Verde in their World Cup opener.

Among European nations, only Spain in June 2009 (15), France in February 2004 (14), Italy in July 2021 (13) and Scotland in March 1885 (13) have enjoyed longer runs.

They will also prove tough to beat on home soil. Since England beat them at the Estadio Benito Villamarin in October 2018, Spain have lost just one of 40 home matches in all competitions (W31 D8) – a 2-1 defeat to Switzerland in September 2022.

Spain are unbeaten in their last 22 games in Madrid (W17 D5) since England won 4-2 in February 1987 thanks to four Gary Lineker goals at the Santiago Bernabeu.

It also looked likely they will have one of their talismanic figures in Lamine Yamal back, after the 19-year-old missed the Czechia clash with a knee injury.

Luis de la Fuente seemed optimistic he would have the teenage sensation available when they face England, whom Yamal scored against in September, finding the back of the net within the first two minutes.

Spain have scored fewer goals than England (14 to 16), but not for lack of trying, with La Roja firing off 22 shots against Czechia, their highest total in a Nations League match in the 2026-27 campaign.

No matter what, Spain will not want to halt their unbeaten streak, especially not in front of their home fans, and De la Fuente's side will be determined to hit their top level.

For England, Thursday was all about Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane.

He made a record-breaking 126th appearance for England, overtaking Peter Shilton as their most-capped player, and his penalty proved to be the winner against Croatia.

After that match, he spoke of his desire to clinch top spot in the group, and he will likely be key to England's bid if they want to get the better of the World Cup winners.

The England captain did score in the reverse fixture at Wembley but also missed a penalty while the Three Lions were 2-1 up, with Spain launching a comeback shortly after.

Overall, he has scored in each of his last five games for England – the fifth time he has had a run of at least five games netting for the national team – and has netted in his last six Nations League outings.

Kane has scored in each of his last six away appearances for England, though, netting nine goals.

#1787. Sheffield Wednesday vs Plymouth Argyle - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sam Varley | 12 Nov 2026 20:15

Sheffield Wednesday will play their first League One game under the management of Dave Challinor on Saturday, when they welcome Plymouth Argyle to Hillsborough.

A four-match winless streak has seen the hosts drop to ninth spot in the League One table, but they only trail the fifth-placed visitors by three points.

Sheffield Wednesday return to action at the weekend aiming to end a winless run and get up and running under new manager Dave Challinor.

Enjoying a fresh start under new ownership after administration and relegation in 2025-26, the Owls quickly got up and running under Henrik Pedersen, staking their claim for an immediate return to the Championship by earning 18 points from their first nine games courtesy of five wins and just one defeat.

They have since gone winless in four league games and six in all competitions, though, with 2-0 away losses to Notts County and Doncaster Rovers spelling the end of Pedersen's tenure before Matt Hamshaw took temporary charge and oversaw league draws against Cambridge United and Blackpool.

The Owls hierarchy then turned to Dave Challinor to take the reins, with his spell beginning with consecutive cup games, as the South Yorkshire side firstly lost 2-1 after extra time to Oldham Athletic in the FA Cup, having levelled through Davis Keillor-Dunn, before taking a 4-0 EFL Trophy beating from fourth-tier Accrington Stanley on Wednesday at Hillsborough with a heavily rotated team.

Yet to get going under Challinor, but now with full focus on bouncing back in their League One promotion bid, Sheffield Wednesday sit ninth and two points outside of the playoffs and will bid to end their rut with a victory at Hillsborough to move level with the visitors.

Their opponents, meanwhile, make the long trip to South Yorkshire aiming to build on consecutive cup wins and a four-game unbeaten streak.

Aiming to build on a strong end to the 2025-26 League One season, in which they fell just short of the playoffs after a poor start, Plymouth Argyle currently find themselves fifth having earned 23 points from their first 14 outings, winning seven and losing five of those.

In a tight top end of the table, the Pilgrims lost ground with consecutive defeats in October, losing 2-0 and 3-0, but they bounced back with a hard-fought 3-2 away win at Cambridge United, thanks to an own goal and finishes from Xavier Amaechi and Aribim Pepple, before playing out a goalless stalemate with Reading.

Tom Cleverley's side have also since been in consecutive cup games heading into the weekend, firstly cruising past Alvechurch in the FA Cup first round before Seb Campbell scored a 99th-minute winner in a 2-1 EFL Trophy triumph over Swindon Town on Tuesday.

Now sitting fifth, but only three points above their ninth-placed hosts and just three behind second-placed Stockport County, they can quickly improve their standing at the top end of the division by extending their run in the coming weeks starting with a victory at Hillsborough.

Sheffield Wednesday form (all competitions):

Sheffield Wednesday will likely remain without goalkeepers Joe Lumley and Ashley Maynard-Brewer, meaning Connal Trueman should again deputise between the sticks.

Reece James, Liam Cooper, Louie Barry, Tyler Onyango, Ali Al-Hamadi and Mason Burstow may all remain confined to the treatment room, while Billy Mitchell has also missed the last three games.

Davis Keillor-Dunn has scored in his last two appearances and will play an important role in the attack, while the likes of Harry Gray, Jamal Lowe and Kieran Morrison will also compete for spots with Callum Slattery likely to come back in from the outset in support after resting for the EFL Trophy match.

Plymouth Argyle have a relatively clean bill of health, other than Joe Edwards who is sidelined.

The Pilgrims rotated heavily for their midweek EFL Trophy tie, and Will Evans and Aribim Pepple should both return from the start in attack having scored five and eight goals respectively so far this term.

Xavier Amaechi may rejoin them in a front three, depending on the shape Cleverley opts for, but Oliver Irow and Ronan Curtis also have claims to start, while Tyreeq Bakinson and Harvey White could reform their midfield partnership.

Sheffield Wednesday possible starting lineup:

Trueman; Santos, Weaver, Bernard; Valery, Bannan, Heskey, M Lowe; Slattery; Keillor-Dunn, J Lowe

Plymouth Argyle possible starting lineup:

Storer; Harding, Pleguezuelo, Mitchell, Hartridge; Amaechi, White, Bakinson, Irow; Pepple, Evans

Sheffield Wednesday have not had the dream start under Challinor, but we are yet to see him take charge of a league game at full strength.

The Owls have the quality to at least match their fifth-placed hosts and we anticipate a tight contest at Hillsborough which could end level.

#1786. A failed spell at Wolves almost saw him walk away from football ...now Danny Armstrong is idolised in Romania as he attempts to lead Dinamo Bucharest back to former glories

Published: 13:42 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 13:52 EST, 9 November 2026

The daughter says: ‘Da’. Darby Armstrong, all of two years old, is not calling out for her father, Danny.

‘She is saying “Yes” in Romanian. She can count to ten in Romanian,’ says her proud father. She may have to learn to count higher, and quickly, to chart her father’s figures in the Superliga with Dinamo Bucharest.

Armstrong sits in an upmarket restaurant in the beautiful suburbs of Bucharest with a park stretching towards a lake. He sips ginger tea with honey and engages with waiters, diners and children who approach him for a chat and a photograph.

‘Darby is a bit bemused by it,’ he says. ‘We were in the mall there and a guy wanted a pic. I could see her looking up to see what all the fuss was about.’

Armstrong could be forgiven for being ever so slightly bemused himself. At 29, he has taken a few dunts and not just from enthusiastic full-backs. Success has hardly been overnight.

‘I nearly gave up once,’ he says quietly. ‘Another time I thought it was all over and I was looking at one-to-one coaching or being a personal trainer.’

Danny Armstrong is hailed after his match-winning heroics in a crucial win over UTA Arad

He survived, though. He is a hero at Dinamo. There is a clamour on matchday when he comes out of the tunnel. The ultras, high behind a goal, chant his name with a fervour that suddenly breaks out in red flares and manic jumping.

It is a long way from Ayr. Armstrong knows he did not walk it alone. His saviours include John McGlynn, who brought him to Raith Rovers, George Cairns, who convinced him to stay at Hamilton, and Scott Sellars, the youth coach who advised him to leave Wolverhampton Wanderers for first team football.

He also took inspiration from many team-mates, including Kieran Tierney who was once his room-mate in a Scotland under-age team,

‘I was meant to be rooming with another left-back but he pulled out and this young player from Celtic came in,’ recalls Armstrong. ‘He wasn’t even in the squad initially and now he is Scotland’s best left-back alongside Robbo.

‘I used to play against KT so many times and I have great respect for him, playing so many games for Celtic, getting that move to Arsenal and coming back to Scotland to win trophies. The setbacks he has had… he’s an inspiration.

‘He has resilience. He has motivation. He took the half opportunity that was offered to him and ran with it.’

Armstrong has done the same in Bucharest. He has been bolstered by his past. ‘It builds you,’ he says of his experience. ‘There have been tough spells but you can look back and make sense of them and see how they have helped you. Football takes a lot of work.’

Armstrong has thrived in Romania since making the leftfield switch to Dinamo Bucharest

It takes a lot of belief too. That can be a capricious quality, seemingly dependent on the winds of fortune.

Armstrong can point to two hat-tricks that gave him faith in a time of need. ‘I scored a hat-trick for Hamilton in a youth game at Auchenhowie against Rangers,’ he says. ‘That came after I had been convinced to stick at it.’

He also scored three last season in the derby against Steaua. ‘That was crazy,’ he says. ‘I don’t think I have realised even yet how big it was. People tell me it was the greatest day in their lives. We hadn’t beaten them in five or six years. We were also in a bad spot with poor form. And then I score three. It gives me goosebumps even now.’

He adds: ‘There is a real football culture here. It means so much to people and I love that. It actually wasn’t too hard to come here because I had looked at it a year earlier but stayed on at Kilmarnock. When Dinamo came in and showed me videos and talked about the history, I was on board.’

There was one decisive factor. ‘I knew it was time to try to make a name for myself somewhere else. I wanted to test myself, keep myself open to other opportunities, try to get to the highest level I can get.’

He is professionally coy about the prospect of international football, having again missed out on Sebastien Pocognoli’s latest Scotland squad. He maintains the line of concentrating on his club form, having a dream to play for his country, and hoping to be noticed.

Armstrong was a big hit at Kilmarnock and has long been mooted for a Scotland call-up

His performances in Romania, though, have been so outstanding that there may be the odd glance from the Pocognoli camp at just what is happening at Dinamo. They may have to be quick as Armstrong qualifies for Ireland too.

He plays in a wide right role, with the freedom to cut inside and become a playmaker. His manager, Nuno Campos, has faith in him. He is the latest in a line of characters who have led him from doubt to conviction.

There is no hesitation. ‘It was McGlynn who saved me,’ says Armstrong. But there were previous tribulations that required the intervention of football folk and Armstrong is immensely grateful.

‘I had been going up to Hamilton from Ayr every night as a kid, playing at the weekend, and by the time I was about 15 I think I was drained. I felt I was missing out on other things in life. It was tough on my parents, too, who did everything for me. The family always sacrificed themselves for me.’

His parents told George Cairns, Hamilton coach, that their son did not want to continue. The reply was instant: ‘Get him up here and I will have a chat with him.’

The crisis passed after this talk and that hat-trick against Rangers. But further tribulations were to come.

Armstrong's relentless drive and enthusiasm have made him a standout player in Romania

Armstrong headed to Wolverhampton Wanderers, spurning an offer by Rangers under Mark Warburton and Davie Weir. ‘That was a mistake,’ he says. He was never near first team football at Wolves though the club wanted to retain him. After a chat with Scott Sellars, he took the chance to leave and start again.

‘That was very, very difficult,’ he says. ‘I did not play from May to November. I was sitting by the phone, urging it to ring with an offer. I had thoughts about packing it all in and going into coaching or being a personal trainer.’

Then an unlikely Superman came to the rescue in the shape of McGlynn, then Raith manager. ‘That changed everything, everything,’ says Armstrong.

A bounce game was organised to assess the player but Armstrong admits the team’s performance was awful. ‘I was very much part of that,’ he says.

He did much better in another friendly but budget considerations meant McGlynn could offer only a nine-game contract. ‘It was a couple of hundred quid a week but it meant everything to me.’ Five goals in nine games led to an extended contract.

‘He is a genius,’ says Armstrong. ‘He is so big on detail, detail, detail. He is a fantastic football coach. It’s an obsession for him.

‘I have never met a man like him. He saved my football career and made me believe I could make it.’

John McGlynn helped save Armstrong's career by taking him under his wing at Raith Rovers

After a spell at Ross County, Armstrong flourished under Derek McInnes at Kilmarnock and the move to Romania offered further scope for growth.

‘It was a bit difficult at first settling in but now my partner, Lauren, and Darby love it. We have made friends,’ he says.

At this a couple of waiters approach the table with grins and cheery banter. Armstrong responds with a warm handshake and that half-embrace that signals another acquiescence to yet another picture.

‘The big difference this season is the coach,’ says Armstrong. ‘He has come in and completely changed the environment and the atmosphere. He has brought fun back and he makes you want to come into training.’

Dinamo are now sitting joint-top of the league. ‘The first goal has to be European football, getting this club back to where it belongs,’ he says.

Armstrong has his sights set on an historic Romanian title and is not ruling out a longer stay

The Dinamo fans, who have not witnessed a league title in 20 years, sense Superliga glory. ‘We are a good side and we play nice stuff,’ says Armstrong. ‘But let’s take it game by game.’

He has the same laid-back attitude to his contract. ‘It expires at the end of the season and there is an option there but we leave all that to after Christmas.’

He is happy in Bucharest but knows the fate of a footballer is never predictable. ‘It is a wonderful place. The fans are great and the manager has faith in me.’

He points out that Campos wants him to be a ‘monster’. This is an instruction to be powerful and innovative in the final third.

The next night Armstrong swivels just outside the box and hits a wonderful shot to open the scoring against UTA Arad.

He then sprints towards the stand where Lauren and Darby are celebrating. He has just been a monster. But he is still a dad, in whatever language.

#1785. England Have Improved Since Berlin – Now Comes the Hard Part

When Thomas Tuchel looks across the touchline in Madrid on Sunday, he will not simply see the reigning world champions. He will see the team that has become England’s reference point over the past few years.

Spain have beaten England in the Euro 2024 final. They have extended an extraordinary unbeaten run. They remain the side that, more often than not, finds the right solution when the margins are finest and the pressure is greatest. If England are serious about becoming tournament winners under Tuchel, they must eventually prove they can do more than compete with Spain. They must show they can beat them. That is the challenge awaiting them in the Nations League decider.

The encouraging news for England is that there are genuine signs of progress. The uncomfortable reality is that progress and victory are not always the same thing.

One of the striking features of England’s recent encounters with Spain is that they no longer feel overawed by them.

The Euro 2024 final exposed deficiencies in England’s ability to manage elite opposition over the course of ninety minutes. Spain controlled key phases of the contest and ultimately deserved their victory. When the teams met again at Wembley earlier in this Nations League campaign, however, the contest felt markedly different.

England lost 3-2, but they also produced periods of football that genuinely unsettled Spain. There were phases when Tuchel’s side pressed aggressively, attacked with conviction and looked capable of taking the game away from their opponents. According to Tuchel, Harry Kane’s missed penalty at 2-1 represented a pivotal moment because England had established significant momentum and were in a position to extend their advantage. Had that opportunity been converted, the complexion of the match might have changed entirely.

That does not mean England were unfortunate to lose. Spain still created better chances overall and once again demonstrated their ability to remain calm when the game became chaotic. It does suggest, however, that England are moving closer to the level required. The difference between the two sides no longer appears structural or insurmountable. Instead, it increasingly comes down to small moments, concentration and execution.

Perhaps the biggest change under Tuchel has been psychological.

There is a greater willingness to take risks. England’s attacking players appear to have more freedom, and individuals such as Jude Bellingham, Anthony Gordon and Morgan Rogers have benefited from a more proactive approach. England are creating more situations in which their athleticism, pace and attacking quality can influence elite opposition.

The concern is that the same approach has often left them vulnerable.

Tuchel’s side continue to make costly defensive mistakes. Against Spain at Wembley, several of the goals they conceded stemmed from their own errors. Croatia’s recent equaliser also arrived following a defensive lapse. Even before that, England’s exit against Argentina at the World Cup highlighted a recurring issue when facing the very best teams. They frequently produce enough quality to stay in the contest, but too often undermine themselves through moments of poor decision-making.

That explains why Tuchel continues to search for solutions at the back. Injuries have played a role, but the constant changes to England’s defensive partnerships have prevented the sort of continuity that Spain enjoy. While Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham remain fixed points around which the team is built, the defence still feels like an area of ongoing experimentation.

Against lesser opponents, that may be manageable. Against Spain, every weakness tends to be exposed.

What makes Spain such a difficult obstacle is that they possess qualities England are still trying to develop.

Almost every major international side can produce moments of brilliance. Spain combine those moments with control. They understand when to accelerate games and when to slow them down. They cope with adversity without losing their structure. Even significant injuries, including the absence of Rodri for this match, rarely seem to alter their collective identity.

England’s growing confidence means they can now trade punches with Spain. The challenge is sustaining that level over an entire match.

The European champions demonstrated this in Berlin and again at Wembley. There were periods when England looked stronger, more dynamic and more threatening. Yet Spain retained an ability to navigate difficult passages and eventually reassert themselves. That quality is often the difference between excellent international teams and serial winners.

England have made considerable progress under Tuchel, but they have not yet acquired that same aura of inevitability.

The stakes extend beyond finishing top of the group.

For England, this fixture offers an opportunity to measure themselves against the benchmark of international football. Tuchel has spoken repeatedly about wanting to push the limits of the team and test whether they are genuinely evolving. Spain provide the perfect examination because they have consistently answered questions that England have not.

A victory would not erase the pain of previous defeats, nor would it suddenly make England favourites for every tournament they enter. It would, however, represent tangible evidence that this team is beginning to overcome a hurdle that has repeatedly blocked its path.

For several years, England have been close. They reached a European Championship final. They reached a World Cup semi-final. They remain one of the most talented squads in international football. What they have lacked is a signature result against a side of Spain’s calibre when the pressure is highest.

Sunday offers another chance to secure one.

Whether England take it will tell us a great deal about how much progress has really been made under Thomas Tuchel. Spain remain the team to beat. The question England must answer now is whether they have finally become good enough to do exactly that.

The Glazer family reportedly rejected the idea of Eddie Howe becoming Manchester United's new head coach, with the club's majority owners intervening to push Mauricio Pochettino to the top of the managerial shortlist.

Man United sacked Michael Carrick as head coach on Thursday morning, with the Englishman paying the price for the team's poor start to the campaign.

According to the Daily Mail, Man United's director of football Jason Wilcox and the club's CEO Omar Berrada had been pushing for Howe to arrive at Old Trafford.

However, the report claims that the Glazers rejected Howe's arrival and instead insisted that Pochettino should be the number one choice.

Berrada and Wilcox were therefore allegedly both overruled, with the Glazers confident that Pochettino is the best choice at this moment in time.

Pochettino is expected to take charge of USA's two matches during this international period against Haiti before officially beginning work at Man United next Thursday.

As a result, the Argentine will have incredibly limited preparation time for Man United's Premier League clash with Liverpool at Anfield on November 22.

The Glazer family remain in control of the biggest decisions at the club rather than INEOS.

Avram Glazer reportedly signed off on Pochettino's appointment on Wednesday, with Man United agreeing to pay in the region of £7.4m to release the South American from his contract with the USA, which is due to run until 2030.

Avram, who is Man United's co-chairman, is said to have confirmed the decision via a remote call on Wednesday evening, as he is in the United States.

#1782. Liam Scales has no doubt 'amazing' Kasper Hogh will soon bring an end to his worrying Celtic goal drought

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 14:09 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 14:54 EST, 9 November 2026

Liam Scales claims he’s got no fears about Kasper Hogh’s luck turning after the Dane’s goalless run at Celtic extended to 16 matches.

Without a goal to his name since hitting a hat-trick at Kilmarnock on August 9, the forward thought his drought was over when he found the net against the same opponent on Sunday.

Denied his long-awaited moment of glory when VAR spotted an earlier infringement by Mika Baur, Hogh watched from the bench as Martin O’Neill’s side ground out a one-goal win which took them four points clear at the top of the table.

But while the Dane will now have to wait until the home match with St Mirren following the international break for his next opportunity, Scales – the scorer on the day – feels his team-mate has nothing to worry about.

‘He’s been brilliant,’ said the Irishman. ‘He keeps doing the right things and eventually it will fall for him.

‘He was so unlucky with his goal being ruled out. And he told me he was right behind me with the goal I scored. If I’d known that I might have left it!

Liam Scales was Celtic's weekend goal hero but he is tipping Kasper Hogh to come good

‘It will fall for him. He’s a goalscorer and a good player. His all-round game was brilliant, he held the ball up really well.

‘He’s just been unlucky. But his attitude has been brilliant. If he keeps doing the right things it will work out for him.

‘He has an amazing attitude and that’s why I really believe he will be successful.’

With Benjamin Nygren missing a second-half penalty, O’Neill was grateful for the improvised finish of Scales earlier in the game.

‘It took an age to come down,’ Scales recalled of his third of the season. ‘I wasn’t sure if it was going to land on the roof of the net.

‘I was just trying to guide it on target and luckily enough it went in. It was nice to score and hopefully I can get a few more between now and the end of the season.’

The victory over Killie ensured Celtic bounced back from their loss at Falkirk and a draw with Dundee United and built on their dramatic midweek win over Besiktas in the Europa League.

‘It was definitely important,’ said Scales. ‘Two games without a win is bad enough, but three would have been a nightmare.

Hogh thought he had ended his scoring drought at Rugby Park but his effort was ruled out

‘We knew we needed that win and can go into the break and refresh. Some of the lads can rest and recover and hopefully we’ll come back in this form.

‘I do think confidence is a massive part of our group and it was probably hit a little bit. The win against a top side like Besiktas has boosted us a little bit. There’s kind of a better mood around and we just want to keep adding good results.’

Scales is optimistic that the better options that are now at the manager’s disposal can help the side hit the kind of form which has eluded them this season.

‘We had (Hyun-jun) Yang back on Sunday, Jota is obviously starting,’ he said. ‘These guys are getting back to full sharpness and getting minutes. Hopefully, this will help and we can build on it.

‘We know we haven’t been good enough between the last international window and this one. We’ve let a few results go and we’re not exactly where we want to be.

‘We always want to be on top of the table. We don’t want to be chasing. We want to be good arm’s length from the challengers.

‘Last season wasn’t what we wanted at all and we don’t want a repeat of that.’

#1780. Bonera believes Milan Futuro were not ready for first season: “Some thought it was easier”

Daniele Bonera has revisited his time as the head coach of Milan Futuro, revealing his belief that the team wasn’t ready to compete.

The Futuro project was launched ahead of the 2024-25 season to give Milan a ‘second team’ to allow their young talents to develop at a level above that of the Primavera league. They started in Serie C but were relegated in their first season.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The decision was taken to sack Bonera as the head coach given the on-field issues, even though they were competing against experienced sides with a very young side. Massimo Oddo followed him, before the club chose to go with Sergio Navarro this summer, who has the Futuro in third.

Bonera was interviewed by Fanpage and he reflected on that period with the B-team and what he learned from it even despite the rough results, with his comments relayed by MilanNews.

“Milan Futuro was a great opportunity for growth. Perhaps we weren’t clear – and I’m part of this – about the level of Serie C. I had an idea of ​​it, but some thought it was easier,” he said.

“The squad had been built with expectations that were too high compared to what the league is. I don’t think that structure, at that time, was ready to tackle that type of league. On an individual level, however, I felt very comfortable. Starting at home was a positive thing.

“The biggest challenge was understanding which players you actually had available. Some were promoted to the first team, others were dropped, and still others were sent to the Primavera. We had guys who perhaps weren’t playing with us and then came back up.

“From an individual growth perspective, we worked very well in some situations. After a couple of years, we saw the individual value of guys like Camarda, Bartesaghi, Liberali, and Jimenez grow. The value of the players wasn’t in question.

“I think the problem was primarily structural: it’s not always the coach who’s the problem, but the way you do things and the direction you want to take.”

#1779. Jamaica vs Mexico - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 12 Nov 2026 21:10, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 21:11

Jamaica will look to take control of their Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal when they welcome defending champions Mexico to the National Stadium in Kingston in the early hours of Sunday.

The Reggae Boyz finished second in League A Group B after two wins, a draw and a defeat in four group games, while the visitors entered at this stage as the top seed, but they arrive winless in four games under new head coach Rafael Marquez.

Jamaica secured their place in the last eight with a 1-1 draw away to Honduras, and have climbed two places to 69th in the latest FIFA rankings.

Interim head coach Rudolph Speid’s side opened the group with a 3-2 home win over Guatemala, with substitute Renaldo Cephas scoring in stoppage time.

They then lost 1-0 at home to 10-man Honduras, ending a 13-year winless run for the visitors against Jamaica, before Javon East’s brace sealed a 2-0 win at El Salvador, leaving the Reggae Boyz with six goals scored and four conceded in four group matches.

Speid is in the middle of a youth rebuild, and Jamaica have also lost two of their last four home games, while they have not won any of their last six meetings against Mexico (W4, D2), including a 1-0 win at the 2024 Copa America courtesy of Gerardo Arteaga’s 69th-minute goal.

Jamaica did hold Mexico to a 1-1 draw in Kingston in 2022 and led twice in a 2-2 draw at the Estadio Azteca in 2023.

Mexico have not looked like World Cup quarter-finalists since they were knocked out by England in the round of 16 and Javier Aguirre was replaced by Marquez.

The new boss’s first four games, all friendlies in the United States, brought 1-1 draws with Colombia and Peru before a 3-0 defeat to the USMNT and a 2-0 loss to Chile, scoring two goals and conceding seven across the four matches.

El Tri have also lost their last two away quarterfinals in this competition, though the head-to-head record in this fixture still heavily favours them, having won 21 of 29 previous meetings and lost only three.

There is plenty at stake, as the winners over two legs reach the 2027 Nations League Final Four and qualify automatically for the 2027 Gold Cup, while the losers drop into the Gold Cup preliminary round.

Jamaica have several important absentees, as Wrexham striker Bailey Cadamarteri has been left out so he can get minutes at club level, while QPR’s Rumarn Burrell and Coventry’s Ephron Mason-Clark are injured, the latter having hurt himself in training last Thursday.

Kaheem Parris is also out injured, while Leon Bailey, Ian Fray and Di’Shon Bernard missed out over match-fitness concerns, as all three have only recently returned from injury.

Ethan Pinnock also misses out, as Miguel Freckleton comes into the squad at left centre-half.

Andre Blake leads a 23-man squad that includes Damion Lowe, Joel Latibeaudiere, Javon East, Renaldo Cephas and Tyreece Campbell.

Mexico have called up 28 players, and Julian Quinones returns after scoring four goals at the World Cup, while Alexis Vega is also back after hinting at international retirement. ‘

Jesus “Tecatito” Corona returns for the first time since June 2022, and Osijek striker Armando Leon has his first senior call-up.

Raul Jimenez is out after knee surgery, while 18-year-old Gilberto Mora has recovered from the injury that forced him out of the last camp.

Blake; Lowe, King, Freckleton, Webster; Anderson, Ming, Clarke; East, Dixon, Campbell

Padilla; Alvarez, Montes, Vasquez, Gallardo; Lira, Romo, Sanchez; Alvarado, Gimenez, Quinones

Later in the episode, Haaland called a host of famous faces, including Oasis singer Noel Gallagher and former City manager Pep Guardiola, to get their opinions on his transformation.

Pep Guardiola's reaction to Erling Haaland's new haircut. 😭😂📲 Watch: https://t.co/4KvxC9e5mx pic.twitter.com/QQBCKKpGkP

Haaland, 26, has not sported short hair since his time at Borussia Dortmund, where he played three seasons before joining City in 2022.

Haaland removed his hairband during a 4-1 win over Arsenal in 2023 on a raucous night at the Etihad as City beat their title rivals to move one step closer to winning the league. There will be no need for one now, though, with a close-cut look to mark a new campaign.

“I’ll try to find a new Rodri – it is what it is,” the former Chelsea manager said. “Rodri, before he arrived here, he didn’t win the Ballon d’Or, he didn’t win the Champions League, he didn’t win the Club World Cup. Then he joined the club and then after he achieved many important things. Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri.

“When David Silva was here, everyone was worried - Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. When Sergio Agüero was here, everyone was worried – Erling [Haaland] arrived. When Ferdinando left, Rodri arrived. It’s just about this.

“When they leave, you need to be good and recruit the next one. They are all similar – David, Kevin, Fernandinho, Rodri, Agüero, Erling. It’s just normal, it’s a change. It’s not a problem, just go again and try to do the right things.”

Maresca added: “Hopefully we can do the things that we need to do. It doesn’t help that there are players that for different reasons want to leave, this is for sure.

“But we need to adapt and we don’t want to keep players here that don’t want to stay.

“The normal thing in transfer windows is that you have to wait because all the clubs try to keep players until the last week and then sell for more money.

“It’s normal, I’m not worried about that. When the transfer window closes and we have all the squad there, for sure it will be different.”

#1775. Liverpool rival Aston Villa for 17-year-old Ligue 1 breakout star

By Naim Beneddra | 12 Nov 2026 21:47

Liverpool and Aston Villa are reportedly monitoring highly rated Le Havre defender Djibril Ouziad, who could leave the Ligue 1 club next summer despite signing a long-term contract just two months ago.

The 17-year-old has emerged as one of the few bright spots in an otherwise disastrous campaign for the French side, establishing himself in the first team while Le Havre struggle at the bottom of the table.

According to Get French Football News, both Premier League clubs are keeping a close eye on Ouziad's development following his rapid breakthrough in France.

The report also suggests that the teenager is likely to leave Le Havre in the summer of 2027, regardless of whether the Normandy club manage to avoid relegation.

That prospect is particularly striking given that Ouziad only signed his first professional contract in September, committing his future to Le Havre until June 2030.

There is no indication that Liverpool or Aston Villa have submitted an offer, but the defender's emergence has already placed him on the radar of clubs competing in the Champions League.

Ouziad has made an immediate impression during his first season of senior football, featuring in nine Ligue 1 matches and starting eight of them.

Primarily deployed as a right wing-back, the French teenager is also capable of playing in a more conventional right-back role.

His performances have been particularly encouraging considering Le Havre's difficult circumstances.

The club have failed to win any of their opening 10 league matches, collecting just two points while suffering eight defeats.

That disastrous start resulted in the dismissal of Didier Digard, with former Crystal Palace and Blackburn Rovers defender Valerien Ismael appointed as his replacement.

Le Havre have also experienced significant upheaval behind the scenes, with president Jean-Michel Roussier and sporting director Demba Ba leaving the club following disagreements surrounding its management.

Despite that instability, Ouziad has continued to develop and has already been rewarded with international recognition.

The defender made his debut for France's Under-18 side earlier this season, further strengthening his reputation as an emerging talent.

His early progress has reportedly caught the attention of Liverpool and Aston Villa, although neither club is known to have opened formal negotiations.

For Liverpool, the link comes as the club continue assessing their defensive options under Andoni Iraola.

The Reds have previously explored reinforcements at right-back, having failed in a late attempt to sign Chelsea's Malo Gusto during the summer transfer window.

Ouziad would represent a considerably less experienced option, and there is no suggestion that Liverpool view him as an immediate solution to their first-team requirements.

Aston Villa's reported interest likewise remains at the monitoring stage, with the French youngster's development likely to be assessed over the coming months.

The most intriguing aspect of Ouziad's situation concerns the timing of a potential departure.

Le Havre secured the defender's first professional contract on September 1, tying him to the club until the summer of 2030.

Yet Get French Football News reports that a transfer at the end of the current campaign is already considered likely, regardless of the club's final position in Ligue 1.

The prediction does not mean Le Havre have decided to sell, nor does it establish that Ouziad is seeking an immediate move abroad.

However, his lengthy contract would give the French side considerable leverage should Liverpool, Aston Villa or another interested club decide to pursue a transfer.

Le Havre would not face the pressure of losing the teenager on a free transfer in the near future, potentially allowing them to demand a substantial fee for one of their most promising academy graduates.

No valuation has been reported, and it remains unclear what figure would persuade the Ligue 1 outfit to negotiate.

Liverpool already have experience of investing in emerging French defenders, having agreed a deal worth approximately £55m to sign Jeremy Jacquet from Rennes earlier this year.

The centre-back subsequently joined Iraola's squad for the 2026-27 season, demonstrating the club's willingness to invest in younger players with significant potential.

Ouziad is at a much earlier stage of his development, however, and his nine senior appearances provide only a limited indication of his long-term prospects.

For now, the teenager's immediate priority remains establishing himself in Le Havre's first team as the club attempts to recover from its miserable start to the season.

His future could nevertheless become an increasingly prominent transfer story if Liverpool or Aston Villa turn their reported interest into a concrete approach ahead of next summer.

#1773. Liverpool vs Arsenal Preview: Team News, Tactics, Lineups and Prediction

Home » Home 2 » Liverpool vs Arsenal Preview: Team News, Tactics, Lineups and Prediction

Table-toppers Arsenal travel to Anfield tonight with their first Premier League trophy since the ‘invincibles’ season of 2004 in sight. The Gunners top the table and with stuttering performances from Manchester City and a Leicester City whose fairytale run seems at an end, and are in pole position to finish the current campaign as champions.

While Jurgen Klopp’s men are still finding their way inconsistently since his appointment, Arsenal are in top form with five victories out of their last six matches. In comparison, Liverpool have been as easy to predict as a magic 8 ball, with impressive wins over Leicester City and Manchester City, but accompanied with horrific losses against Watford and West Ham. With fourth place still within grasp and with an impressive record against the table topping teams this season, Liverpool would look to give their long suffering fans some cheer with which to greet this New Year.

The Reds desperately need a victory to steady the ship as their erratic and wayward form sees them enter 2016 still outside the top 4 and distant from any title challenge.

With a host of injuries to his main XI, Jurgen Klopp could be forgiven for dipping into the transfer market so early. The Reds have captured QPR right-back Steven Caulker along with Marko Grujic in the January transfer window.

With Grujic returning to his former club Red Star Belgrade on loan, Steven Caulker is likely to be given a run out as a substitute with the current spate of Liverpool injuries.

Ings, Sturridge, Lovren, Coutinho, Origi and Flanagan are amongst the Liverpool afflicted and will take no part in the match ahead. With Lovren out, Kolo Toure and Mamadou Sakho look likely to be Klopp’s first choice central defending partnership.

Alberto Moreno and Nathaniel Clyne should start as full-backs for the Liverpool side and will be crucial in any attempt to penetrate the Gunner’s defences. Emre Can and Lucas should marshal the midfield, while James Milner, Firmino and Adam Lallana look to give Petr Cech some concerns about his goal. Leading the line should be Christian Benteke, who’s lack of form doesn’t threaten this match as manager Klopp has few options in his position.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Mignolet; Clyne, Sakho, Toure, Moreno; Lucas, Can, Firmino, Lallana, Milner, Benteke.

Arsenal must show that they have the one quality required of all champions : Consistency. The task is hereby straightforward for Wenger’s men. Win, keep winning, regardless of your manner and the title is yours.

With half the season concluded, Arsene Wenger must be wishing that he received a Christmas gift from the Arsenal medical team. Injuries have decimated his midfield with Wilshire, Cazorla, Rosiscky, Coquelin and Sanchez out of the game.

There is some good news with Mesul Ozil having managed to partake in some leisure instead of participating in the FA cup victory over Sunderland. Keeping the nimble playmaker fit would be key to Arsenal aspirations, both in this match and for the remainder of the season.

With both Petr Mertersacker and Gabriel available, it would be interesting to see whom Arsene Wenger picks out for his starting XI. Koscielny, Bellerin and Monreal have nailed down their place in the defence and the inclusion of the slower Mertersacker or the inconsistent Gabriel may have a defining moment in the game.

With Arsenal’s midfield woes, it should fall to Flamini to screen the defence with Ramsey alongside him. Walcott, Ozil and Joel Campbell should be the main thrusts of Arsenal’s attacking play with Giroud as the elegant, decisive focus.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Cech; Bellerin, Gabriel, Koscielny, Monreal; Flamini, Ramsey, Ozil, Walcott, Campbell; Girourd.

With previous encounters between these teams resulting in high scoring draws, we favour a repeat of last year’s epic 2-2 result for the same fixture. Martin Skrtel’s 97th minute header in front of the Kop capped a memorable game which also had Fabio Borini sent off and we expect similar fireworks at Anfield tomorrow.

#1771. Falkirk boss John McGlynn deserves big move, says Craig Levein, as Aberdeen sack Stephen Robinson

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 17:30 EST, 9 November 2026

Craig Levein believes John McGlynn ‘ticks every box’ to manage a bigger club than Falkirk — as Aberdeen begin the search for Stephen Robinson’s successor.

The Northern Irishman was sacked last night after eight months in charge, with the Dons’ 4-0 home loss to Hibs on Saturday proving to be the last straw.

With the Pittodrie side now sitting second bottom of the Premiership, chairman Dave Cormack, sporting director Lutz Pfannenstiel and newly-appointed chief executive Adrian Bevington will soon begin the process of trying to identify the man they believe can take the team forward.

And Levein, a former Hearts colleague of McGlynn’s, believes the veteran’s record of taking the Bairns from League One to third place in the top flight should speak for itself.

'John has passed every test that’s been put in front of him and I don’t know what he needs to do,’ said Levein.

‘Falkirk supporters, of course, won’t like me saying that, but I’ve worked with the guy. He’s got integrity, knowledge, he delves into the minutiae when he’s doing his team talks and makes sure everybody knows what’s expected.

Falkirk boss John McGlynn has guided them from League One to third in the Premiership

Aberdeen boss Stephen Robinson was sacked after eight months in charge at Pittodrie

‘I’m biased, I like the guy, but I think he’s done a wonderful job. He’s done all the work that he needs to do in my eyes to get an opportunity.’

McGlynn worked at Hearts as a coach under Jim Jefferies and went on to manage the Gorgie club twice — once as an interim.

Prior to taking charge of Falkirk in 2022, he had two spells at Raith Rovers, a stint at Livingston and a scouting role at Celtic under Brendan Rodgers.

Despite completely turning the Bairns’ fortunes around, Levein believes that there remains a strange reluctance in some quarters to recognise the 64-year-old as one of the shrewdest managers in the country.

‘I don’t know what it is, looking at what he’s done, his whole body of work,’ shrugged Levein.

‘When I went to Hearts at the tail end of my career, I was helping John do some training with the youngsters. Even then, you could tell immediately that he knows what he’s talking about.

‘He spent a fair bit of time with Brendan at Celtic. After that, I think he adopted Brendan’s style of football with some changes and altered two or three bits.

‘Essentially, he went to Celtic, watched and learned everything on top of the knowledge he already had. His team at Raith started to play in the same way as Celtic did. Then he’s continued that when he’s gone to Falkirk.

‘I was promoting him for the Scotland job when it came around. If you look at his record, it’s pretty impressive.

‘I just think he is undervalued, maybe not by the supporters that have had him as their manager, but certainly in a wider sense in Scotland. He has done a brilliant job so far.

‘I’ll come back to the fact I’m biased. I like the guy. I like what he does at football clubs. If I’m a chairman, all day long I’d be looking for somebody like him.

‘He’s meticulous in his work and everything’s done properly. He stays within the bandwidth of emotions.

‘He doesn’t get overly emotional during matches and he stays in his area, which I think is good for him and good for his players.

‘You don’t often see him throwing stuff about in the dugout or anything like that. He’s a top manager who has improved enormously in the last five or six years.’

Craig Levein believes McGlynn has done more than enough to merit a move to a bigger club

Robinson’s departure was confirmed yesterday in a statement.

Despite winning the League Cup with St Mirren a year ago and guiding the Buddies to three straight top-six finishes, he never enjoyed a consistent run of results at Pittodrie.

‘Following a board meeting, Aberdeen Football Club has today taken the decision to part company with head coach Stephen Robinson,’ the statement read.

‘Stephen leaves the club alongside assistant head coach Brian Kerr and first team coach Stephen Craigan. We thank them for their efforts during their time at Pittodrie and wish them every success for the future.

‘Preparatory work to support the appointment of a new manager has been undertaken, and the recruitment process is ongoing. The focus will be on identifying the right candidate to lead the club forward and deliver the progress expected across all areas of the football operation.

‘Stuart Duff will assume interim charge of first team training while the club continues its search for a new head coach.’

With many runs expected infield, Walker and Davies will have to stay on their toes to keep a tab on the two. Drinkwater and Kante will be the two preferred central midfield players. Drnkwater with the role of play making and Kante to provide cover for the back four, similar to Dier.

It must be noted that Kanteai??i??s inclusion is crucial as the Frenchman has made 79 tackles and 81 interceptions, the highest in the League this season. Okazaki and Ulloa will continue to play as the two strikers as Jamie Vardy can be expected only to come off the bench.

Predicted Line-up: Schmeichel; Fuchs, Huth, Morgan, Simpson; Albrighton, Kante, Drinkwater, Mahrez; Okazaki, Ulloa.

Harry Kane was briefly rested in the previous game, where he was introduced in the dying minutes in search of an equaliser. This shows how reliant the Tottenham side are on Kane for goals.

Nevertheless back into the squad, the tireless striker will look to get his name in the score sheet as many times as possible in order to allow Spurs to gain all three points. With his extremely high work rate, Kane averages a stunning 2.65 shots per game. With just 4 goals shy of his competitors Vardy and Lukaku, the Englishman will look catch up to his competitors.

With both sides fielding their best players available, the level of the game will be higher than that fans witnessed in the weekend. However, with Kane and Alli in the squad as well as a change to the back four, Tottenham will be a force to reckon with, Although the inclusion of Vardy will bring Leicester a goal inclusion of the Belgian duo at center back and captain Lloris in the squad will make it tougher for Leicester to outscore Tottenham.

#1769. Algeria vs Togo - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 12 Nov 2026 21:57

Algeria host Togo at the Stade Hocine Ait Ahmed on Saturday, knowing that victory could strengthen their position at the top of Group I in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers.

The Desert Foxes lead the standings with four points from their opening two matches, one point ahead of the third-placed Sparrowhawks, who trail second-placed Zambia on goal difference, setting up an important double-header between the two nations.

Algeria have made a solid start under Brahim Hemdani, who remains unbeaten in his three matches in charge since September following Vladimir Petkovic's departure in August.

Petkovic's final game at the helm was a defeat to Switzerland in the World Cup round of 32, but Hemdani has since overseen a 3-1 victory over Zambia in the opening fixture of the AFCON qualifiers before his side recovered from two goals down to earn a 2-2 draw at Burundi on matchday two.

Algeria have now scored at least twice in three consecutive matches, including a 2-1 friendly victory over Niger in Tizi Ouzou in October, when Mohamed Belloumi and Ramy Bensebaini turned the game around after the North Africans conceded in the first half.

While that result extended the Desert Foxes’ impressive run, it also highlighted their recent defensive problems, having conceded 13 goals in their last seven matches across all competitions without keeping a clean sheet.

However, the hosts have kept Togo at bay in four of their last five meetings and won six of the most recent seven encounters between the sides across friendlies and competitive matches, which should give them confidence heading into Saturday's contest.

Togo are bidding to reach the AFCON finals for the first time since 2017 and made a winning start to their qualifying campaign by beating Burundi 1-0 in Lome, thanks to a goal from Dermane Karim.

However, Patrice Neveu's side failed to build on that success, suffering a 2-0 defeat away to Zambia on matchday two, which brought their six-match unbeaten run across all competitions to an end.

The defeat also marked the first time Togo had failed to score in six outings this year, since their goalless draw against South Africa in October 2025 during the final round of the World Cup qualifiers, where they finished fourth in Group B.

Currently 120th in the FIFA World Rankings, Les Eperviers face a difficult task against an Algeria side ranked 92 places higher, with Saturday's encounter also marking the first leg of a demanding double-header before the teams meet again in Lome three days later.

Togo also have a poor away record to overcome heading into this weekend’s clash, having managed just one victory in their last 13 matches outside their home country (D6, L6), dating back to a 2-1 friendly win over Niger in March 2024.

Algeria Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Togo Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Algeria will be without Hull City winger Bachir Belloumi, who is recovering from a hamstring injury, while Brighton & Hove Albion defender Jaouen Hadjam and Hicham Boudaoui have also withdrawn through injury.

Amin ?hiakha and Rafik Belghali have also withdrawn from camp due to fitness issues, while Fahem Benaissa-Yahia has been called up to replace Hadjam and Adem Zorgane takes Boudaoui's place.

Yacine Titraoui has returned to the squad after missing the previous camp, while Mohamed Azzi and Abderrahmane Rebbach have received their first senior call-ups. Manchester City defender Rayan Ait-Nouri and Luca Zidane are among the notable omissions.

Togo will be without Sharani Zuberu and Steven Nador due to hamstring injuries, while Mansour Ouro-Tagba is also unavailable.

Lilian Brassier has received his first call-up and could make his debut, while Kennedy Boateng and Thibault Klidje have returned to the squad. Augustin Drakpe has also been recalled after recovering from injury.

Benbot; Azzi, Bensebaini, Nair, Benaissa-Yahia; Bentaleb, Titraoui, Abdelli; Amoura, Gouiri, Maza

Barcola; Brassier, Boateng, Bode, Koudossou; Djene, Karim, Ouro; Komlavi, Djibril, Denkey

Algeria have greater attacking quality and a strong recent record against Togo, and we expect Hemdani's side to make home advantage count with a first-leg victory.
