#1734. 'I've never revealed the whole story': England fans wouldn't boo me if they knew the truth, says Ben White... as he defends World Cup walkout and rejecting call-ups

Published: 15:00 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 18:20 EST, 9 November 2026

Ben White believes England fans would not boo him if they knew the truth behind his 2022 World Cup walkout.

The Arsenal defender left the camp in Qatar after the group stages citing 'personal reasons', although a fallout with Gareth Southgate's assistant, Steve Holland, was later reported. He then declined a return to the England set-up while Southgate and Holland were in charge but was included by Thomas Tuchel in March of this year.

However, White was booed by fans inside Wembley when he came on in the second-half of a friendly against Uruguay, only to score his first international goal and then concede a late penalty in a 1-1 draw. He was not selected for the World Cup in North America but is back with the squad ahead of this week's Nations League fixtures against Croatia and Spain.

And the 29-year-old, addressing those jeers for the first time, said: 'It was hard to hear, especially because they didn't know the situation, which is kind of what I put my mind to.

'They don't know my situation and it is not really about what I have done, because they don't know why, and if they did they would not be booing or saying these things. I just think about maybe (them) not knowing the full story, and if they did, maybe they wouldn't (boo).'

He added: 'Obviously, a load has been said. I've probably seen all of it. I just think people don't know the full story, because I've never said anything, and I won't put anyone under the bus or share any of that.

Ben White has insisted he would not be booed by England fans if they knew the truth behind his World Cup walkout

White fell out with former England assistant Steve Holland (left) before heading home during the 2022 World Cup

'There were loads of things that happened and communication wasn't great. I don't want to throw anyone under the bus. A lot of people try to do that to me so it's something I wouldn't want to do myself. I think it's probably the best way. It's a bit tricky and not straightforward, but it's amazing to be here now. It's a privilege to be called up.'

White, however, is adamant that he would make the same decision today and leave the World Cup, even if he will not divulge the reasons as to why.

'I don't think I would (do anything different),' he said. 'I think, as a person, I'm quite real, and I made the decision that I would probably continue to make. It's one that I'm not happy about. It wasn't ideal. But it happened, it's time to move on.

'I don't think I am looking to win anyone over or say anything that helps them get back on my side. It is what it is. There are reasons for it and I am just looking forward to playing for England and doing well and looking for success.'

White has spoken publicly about not watching football, and this, too, has been used against him by some supporters.

'It doesn't mean I don't like football, because I do it every day, so I must like it a little bit!' he said. 'It's because I don't watch it, which I think is quite normal for someone that does a job and then doesn't go home and then continue watching that job.

'I don't think anyone knows my personality. I keep that to my loved ones and family. It's all noise when people have an opinion on that stuff. It is not actually me. People don't know me and I like it that way. You give so much to the game, which is intense. I think it's important to keep some bits for yourself. I keep the energy for the people I love.'

England new boy Josh King believes his aptitude for academia gives him an advantage at the start of a burgeoning career.

The Fulham star – who has two Premier League goals this season – linked up with Thomas Tuchel’s squad on Monday morning as one of two fresh call ups alongside Jobe Bellingham.

King was a straight-A student at the renowned independent Hampton School in south London, with alumni including Queen guitarist Sir Brian May and golf pro Paul Casey.

The teenager’s mother, Michelle, is a university lecturer and finishing a PhD on sickle cell disease while his father Steve is a personal injury lawyer.

‘The most important thing about being good academically and education-wise is you’re able to take on information much more quickly,’ King said.

‘You can take on information which might take a bit longer for other people. I think that definitely helps.’

While the 19-year-old was invited to take part in a pre-World Cup training camp in Miami, he is hoping to make his international bow against Croatia on Thursday.

Although a central figure in Fulham’s midfield, a confident King could be utilised wider by Tuchel were he to be given an opportunity across the two-game Nations League camp.

‘There was a buzz around Fulham when I got called up [this week],’ he added. ‘I got off the phone with the boss, ran into the kitchen and started cheering with my dad. I called mum at work and she was screaming in the office. This felt slightly unachievable when I was younger.’

Jude Bellingham and Harry Kane were namechecked as those who helped him settle when introduced to the group in Florida, with King having also studied the likes of Jamal Musiala and Pedri to elevate his own game.

‘The main thing you take is the standards they set,’ he said when reflecting on joining the camp in America. ‘The way they conduct themselves, the way they perform every day, the way they train and the way they take everything seriously.

‘The little things, technical things, the way some people strike the ball, the way some people pass, just little things which you almost take without thinking about it - they also have an impact.

‘On a few occasions I asked “how do you finish this way” or “what do you do in this scenario” and it always helps to add to my game.’

#1732. Next Man United manager: Neville urges Pochettino to demand three guarantees before taking the job

By Axel Clody | 13 Nov 2026 07:18

Michael Carrick’s departure from the Manchester United dugout, announced on Thursday morning, has paved the way for the possible arrival of Mauricio Pochettino at Old Trafford. With the club 18th in the Premier League, inside the relegation zone, Manchester United are looking for a change of direction to try to avoid an even more complicated situation this season.

Faced with the possibility of taking over the team, however, the Argentine has received a warning from Gary Neville: do not accept the challenge without concrete guarantees from the board.

The former defender believes Pochettino needs to protect himself before taking the job, particularly given the limitations of the squad and the need for an overhaul. For Neville, INEOS must present a clear commitment to the sporting project, both with regard to immediate signings and planned investment for next season.

Appearing on The Overlap, the Sky Sports pundit pointed to three demands he considers fundamental for the manager: a significant compensation clause in case of dismissal, the signing of two centre-backs in the January window, and a guarantee of a minimum budget to strengthen the squad next summer.

Neville’s first concern relates to the Argentine’s job security.

Pochettino would arrive at Manchester United at a time of deep instability, with the team in a delicate position in the table and under pressure for results. The former player therefore argues that the manager should negotiate significant financial compensation if the club’s executives decide to end his work earlier than planned.

‘If I were Mauricio Pochettino right now, I would be protecting myself with everything I have. He will do that through compensation, so put that in your contract. But secondly, he needs two centre-backs in January.’

The need to reinforce the defensive system, in fact, was one of the points most emphasised by the former Manchester United captain.

Neville believes the area has shortcomings incompatible with the ambitions of a club that wants to return to competing for important positions in the Premier League. In his assessment, Pochettino cannot be held responsible for negative results without being given the conditions to fix the problems found in the squad.

The pundit also highlighted the importance of establishing financial planning in advance for the mid-year transfer window. Signing two defenders in January would therefore not be enough: the Argentine would need to be certain he will receive sufficient resources to continue the overhaul in the following months.

‘So he needs to insist on a minimum budget for next summer’s transfers, so that we can turn this situation around. He needs to insist on receiving a budget that matches his proposal. They have to give him that budget, otherwise he should not accept the job.’

To justify the urgency of changes, Neville pointed to the defensive line-up used by Manchester United in their most recent match: the 4-4 draw against Aston Villa. The former player drew attention to the combination of Diogo Dalot, Noussair Mazraoui, Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven, which finished the match as the team’s back four.

In the pundit’s view, the set-up shows the lack of reliable options and the need for investment in the area. The presence of improvised players or players used out of their usual roles also helps gauge the challenge Pochettino will face if he takes charge of Manchester United.

‘I mean, look at the back four he finished with on Sunday: Dalot at left-back, Mazraoui at right-back, Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven. That is probably the worst back four in the Premier League.’

Neville was even more emphatic in showing his disbelief at the state of the squad. For him, it is difficult to find another top-flight team that has finished a match with such a weakened defensive structure.

‘I do not know of any worse back four than that in the Premier League at the moment, if I am watching the games. It is unbelievable that Manchester United finished the game with that back four.’

#1730. Slavia Prague 1-2 Arsenal: Slight concerns but another away day win

Arsenal secured another away win last night, this time in the Champions League beating Slavia Prague 2-1 thanks to goals from Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres.

Mikel Arteta rotated in some areas, with starts for Ben White, Piero Hincapie, Martin Zubimendi, Mikel Merino and Eberechi Eze, but relied too on the foundational stability of Declan Rice with Ezri Konsa and Gabriel behind him. We began in lively fashion, and took an early lead.

David Raya played it long, Gyokeres held it up well and hooked the ball forward, and Madueke’s pace took him beyond the defender and into the box before finishing between the keeper’s legs. Solid play from two players who can sometimes be guilty of fluffing their lines when it comes to those key actions. This time they were spot on.

We had more chances to score. Eze showed nice skills in the box but saw his shot blocked; Gyokeres headed back across goal for Merino but he headed over; the Spaniard saw a shot from distance tipped over, and his smart near post run and a right-footed shot from a Ben White cutback forced the keeper into another decent stop; and there was a brilliant counter and pass from Rice that drifted all the way to the back post without any Arsenal player attacking it for a tap-in.

We did find a second though. Gyokeres combined well with Merino around their box, and when he was played through he opened up his body really well and produced a fine finish from close range and a tight angle to make it 2-0. I don’t think that goal at Fleetwood would have done much for his confidence, this felt much more like the kind of strike he needed to produce – for himself as much as the team.

So, we had a good lead at the break, but this was very much a game of two halves. In the first we had 60% possession, out-shot the opposition by 8 to 2, and passed at nearly 90% success rate. In the second, the tables turned. Slavia Prague took 17 shots to our 4, and our pass success fell to 77%. We were sloppy and untidy, they made a tactical change at half-time which worked well for them, and while we weren’t necessarily under the cosh, the entire dynamic of the game changed and we couldn’t get to grips with it.

We needed David Raya to make one superb save to keep them at bay, before Gabriel had to head one off the line, but in injury time they found the goal I think their second half performance (and ours) probably merited. They whipped in a wicked ball from the left, the striker applied the close range finish, and the clean sheet was gone.

Afterwards, Mikel Arteta was happy with the win, but displeased with the second half, saying:

First of all, you have to value the fact it’s very difficult to win away from home. We’ve done it against a very tough opponent, we expected that toughness. In the first half we played at a really high level in terms of intensity, tempo, quality and clarity in what we had to do, and what the game was demanding. We were very efficient – we should have scored three, four or five.

I already talked about some of the things we didn’t do, and others I’d prefer not to mention. It’s a huge lesson, and we’ll learn from the second half. It’s our third away game in quick succession, and we’re the only team to have played three away games in the Champions League and just one at home – there are a lot of factors – but I don’t like to use that, because in the first half we were at the level we wanted. I take full responsibility for the drop in the second half.

I don’t think the team played well at all in the second half, but I do wonder about how we might have done things differently. For example, I feel like Declan Rice played within himself in that second period, and let me be clear, I understand why. Personally, I think it’s a bit mad he did 90+ minutes in a game like this, even if I accept he and the manager know more about his fitness than any of us. Maybe they need him to be like a steam train, going going going all the time, but when you have options of the quality of Myles Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes on the bench, surely using them in his stead allows the best of two worlds: some rest for Rice, and fresher legs in midfield when the game is tilting in the opposition’s favour.

We have this really strong bench, but I don’t think the changes we made worked particularly well. The question, of course, is if they absolutely needed to. We had a two goal lead until late on, and we secured all three points away from home after a difficult and physically demanding game at Anfield three days previously. I just found the Jekyll and Hyde nature of of the two halves a little concerning, but only a little. Ten of our sixteen games this season have been away from home, we’ve won seven of them, so that’s a decent return, added to by this victory.

Ultimately, this is essentially a forgettable Champions League tie that we came away with three points from. Apparently it was a year to the day since we played Slavia Prague last season too, a game I had/have zero recollection of. Which might say something about me more than anything else, but these kinds of fixtures don’t live long in the memory. They’re grist for the mill in this part of the season, we had a job to do, and we got it done, and now all the focus turns to Hull on Saturday and the three points required there before the Interlull.

We can talk a bit more about this game in an Arsecast a bit later on this morning, before I head to London a bit later on this afternoon. For those who have registered to come to the launch of The 22 tomorrow at Big Red, please remember you can purchase the book via the email sent to you (check your junk folders if you don’t see it), so you can simply come and collect on the night. We can also facilitate sales via credit card etc if you don’t want to do that.

If you purchased via the Patreon pre-sale, those books are not for collection tomorrow, and will be shipped to you in due course. There is also some scope to come along on spec on the night, and we should have copies available but obviously priority goes to those who registered. We will then have a final batch of books going on general sale online on Saturday evening after the Hull game. Full details of that to follow here on site and via Arseblog on BlueSky.

Ok, I’ll leave it there for now. Pod will be out mid-morning, until then, have a good one.

Welcome to another episode of the Arsecast – the original Arsenal podcast.

In this episode I’m joined by Tom Canton of The Gooner Talk to discuss Arsenal’s 2-1 win over Slavia Prague in the Champions League on Wednesday night. The first half had plenty of positives, not least a goal for Noni Madueke, as well as an assist and a well taken goal for Viktor Gyokeres who put in his best performance of the season so far. #1728. Is the Gyokeres iron hot enough for Hull?

I’m here for our book launch which takes place tonight, but also for our game against Hull tomorrow. Mikel Arteta will meet the press this afternoon ahead of that one, and we’ll bring you all the stories on Arseblog News. I don’t think there’s gonna be anything mind-blowing, it looked like we came through the Slavia Prague game without any issues, so fingers crossed that’s the case.

I suppose I’m mildly curious as to whether Viktor Gyokeres’ performance on Wednesday will see him keep his place up front. He got a great goal, provided an assist for Noni Madueke, and probably should have had another assist when he headed back across goal for Mikel Merino, only for the Spaniard to head over the bar when we know he can do better from those situations.

He’s a player who seems to need confidence and rhythm, and on that basis it would make some sense to keep him in the starting line-up. After the last Interlull, when he scored in four successive games for Sweden, I made the case that giving him a start in our first game back would make some sense to try and harness some of what was a good goal scoring run. Strike while the iron is hot and all that.

I looked at a home game against Leeds as the kind of fixture that would suit him. He scored two against them at home last season, and one at Elland Road, but when the time came Mikel Arteta picked Kai Havertz up front. Speaking about the decision to start Gyokeres on Wednesday in Prague, the manager said:

It was a game we believed would be really good for him, for the demands the opponent puts in and the spaces he could use. He’s done it really well, not just for the assist and the goal, but he was really connected to the team. It’s really great news for him, because he really needed that performance.

The question will be does Arteta think Hull at home will be as good for him as Slavia Prague away? After a bright start to the season they haven’t won any of their last seven but they have drawn five of those. Chances are they’re going to come and sit deep, using the blueprint we’ve seen many teams deploy against Arsenal in the past. If a Gyokeres game, if we can call it that, requires the opposition to leave spaces he can use (as per Arteta’s quote above), then maybe this isn’t one of those.

However, on paper, and with all due respect to tomorrow’s opposition, if Hull at home isn’t a Gyokeres game, then it’s hard not to be a bit worried. Personally, I’d be all right to see him start this one, and if it doesn’t work then you have other options. Havertz is the obvious one, but Mikel Merino is an alternative as well with his ability to find spaces inside the opponent’s penalty area. Ideally though, it’s a bit of a building block of a game for the Swedish international. We need him to deliver goals and assists, the last few weeks have been a bit more positive in that regard, and ultimately it’s important that the manager recognises the moments in a season when he might have to choose one player over another for the overall benefit of the team.

Which is to say, I look forward very much to seeing Declan Rice starting up front against Hull tomorrow, and Arteta revealing that his tech-boffins have invented a gizmo which will allow Rice to player 180 minutes in every game. Plus injury time. I kid, obviously, but I suppose we should know by now that regardless of what we think about team selections, use of players, and everything else, this manager will never be even remotely swayed by external noise – and that’s a good thing most of the time!

We will talk a bit more about the Hull game in a quick preview podcast on Patreon a little later on. Because of the book launch, we’ll be recording before the manager meets the press, so bear that in mind.

Hopefully catch lots of you later on at Big Red – and here’s a nice piece on the photos in the book. Just a reminder again that those who have registered to come to the launch, you can purchase the book via the email sent to you (check your junk folders if you don’t see it), so you can simply come and collect on the night. We can also facilitate sales via credit card etc if you don’t want to do that.

If you purchased via the Patreon pre-sale, those books are not for collection tomorrow, and will be shipped to you in due course. There is also some scope to come along on spec on the night, and we should have copies available but obviously priority goes to those who registered. We will then have a final batch of books going on general sale online on Saturday evening after the Hull game. Full details of that to follow here on site and via Arseblog on BlueSky.

By Lewis Blain | 13 Nov 2026 07:19

Manchester United are targeting Villarreal right-back Alex Freeman as Mauricio Pochettino prepares to take charge at Old Trafford.

The 22-year-old has impressed in LaLiga and established himself as an important member of the United States national team under the Argentine.

With Diogo Dalot struggling for consistency, Freeman could offer United a significant upgrade at right-back.

According to reports, Freeman has emerged as a transfer target for United and several European clubs after a breakthrough in 2026, having progressed from Orlando City's youth system to becoming Villarreal's first-choice right-back.

The American made nine appearances following his January move to Spain and has featured 16 times across all competitions in 2026-27, including four outings in the Champions League.

His development has also been recognised internationally, with Freeman starting four of the USA's five matches at the 2026 World Cup over the summer.

Pochettino is clearly an admirer, having previously described the 26-cap defender as a player with the potential to become one of the best in his position in the world.

The report also suggests that Manchester City and Tottenham are also interested, but United could have an advantage when Pochettino takes over at Old Trafford.

Dalot has started eight of United's ten Premier League matches this season, but his performances have attracted criticism, with supporters booing him following the 4-4 draw against Aston Villa.

His defensive mistakes have contributed to United's problems at the back, with the Portuguese being part of a defence that hasn't kept a clean sheet this season, and he has struggled to provide the consistency expected of a regular starter.

Freeman could offer a different profile. Standing at 6 foot 2, he combines physical presence with impressive technical ability, ranking in the 94th percentile for duels won, and the 93rd for aerial duels won. He also ranks in the 100th percentile for recoveries.

Those figures suggest he could bring greater defensive authority without compromising United's ability to build attacks from the back.

At 22, Freeman also represents a longer-term investment, while his versatility allows him to cover at centre-back if required.

Pochettino's previous relationship with the defender could make United an attractive destination, and a January move would address an area that clearly needs strengthening.

#1726. Champions League draw: Arsenal to renew Mourinho rivalry with Real Madrid tie

Arsenal will host old nemesis José Mourinho’s Real Madrid in the league phase of the Champions League.

Mourinho, the former Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur manager, will return to London to resume hostilities against last season’s beaten finalists.

Other reunions from Thursday’s draw include Manchester City travelling to Barcelona, to whom they last week sold Rodri, and Liverpool visiting Inter Milan, who have signed Curtis Jones.

Arsenal will also travel to Harry Kane’s Bayern Munich, while United will host the Germans as well on their Champions League return in a repeat of the legendary 1999 final. Michael Carrick’s side will also visit Cesc Fàbregas’s Como.

Mourinho last managed at the Emirates Stadium in March 2021, barely a month before his sacking by Spurs.

During his two spells as Chelsea manager, Mourinho famously had run-ins with Arsenal’s Arsène Wenger.

Mourinho called Wenger a “specialist in failure” after the Frenchman failed to add to his three Premier League titles following his Portuguese counterpart’s arrival in London in 2004.

Last season, Mikel Arteta finally ended Arsenal’s long wait to be crowned champions of England but agonisingly missed out on European glory.

Verdict Premier League champions should not be daunted by any game, but Real Madrid – with Mourinho in control – has the feel of a defining match of the group stage. Facing Kane in Munich does not seem any easier. Some tough assignments here including a trip to Napoli but the pot-four teams seem straightforward for Mikel Arteta.

Verdict Playing against the European champions and travelling to Barcelona will be a true test of how much progress Enzo Maresca has made in the short time he has been at the Etihad Stadium. City’s other games do not look easy either but they should be defeating teams such as Sporting Lisbon and Porto – at least they would be expected to under Pep Guardiola.

Verdict The San Siro was where Arne Slot began to turn results around last season and Iraola getting a win there would be a big statement. Atlético staged a comeback at Anfield in 2020 and the repeat fixture will be tight. But there are enough winnable games there for Liverpool to reach the next round.

Verdict They will face a wall of noise in Istanbul when they play Galatasaray, but Villa will look to get points from the game. There are some tasty destinations for travelling fans and getting results there will ease the pressure on the match against PSG, who have been rattled by Villa before but remain a difficult opponent. The Nou Camp is a place where momentum can change in a season – for good or bad.

Verdict The repeat of the 1999 final is the standout fixture, but Michael Carrick should be looking beyond that match for the points needed to progress. He has been given a tough set of away games to navigate. They are winnable but difficult. So those games at Old Trafford will be very important.

That brings our coverage of the Champions League draw to an end, as the 36 teams found which eight teams they will be facing in the league phase of this season’s tournament. Thanks for joining us!

The league phase will kick off on 8 September and will be wrapped up after all teams play at the same time on 27 January.

The top eight teams of the league phase progress to the last 16 automatically, while teams that finish between ninth and 24th will be forced to navigate a play-off tie to reach the knockout stages.

Marquinhos is not at the ceremony, so it will be PSG president Nasser Al-Khelaifi coming up to collect it. We hear from the defender on a video message.

#1725. GdS: The ‘dream’ and two alternatives – Milan draw up three-man centre-back wish list

AC Milan are in the market for a new central defender ahead of the winter window, and three names are on the list.

According to La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below), Gerry Cardinale wants to give Ruben Amorim at least two signings in January. One of them will be a centre-forward – with Nicolo Tresoldi the ambitious idea at the moment – while the other will be a defender.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

With Matteo Gabbia sidelined until well into January and Fikayo Tomori currently injured, Amorim has been juggling an emergency in recent weeks. It was a situation further compounded by an issue that arose for Strahinja Pavlović last week.

Fortunately for Amorim, he has found a capable alternative in the youngster Sankhoun Diawara. Looking ahead, however, the club is considering an addition that could immediately boost the level of the department.

A summer target was Gonçalo Inácio whom Amorim knows well, having coached him for years at Sporting CP. Dialogue with the Lisbon club has continued even during the current period when the transfer window is closed, following the failure to reach an agreement before.

Milan could renew their pursuit soon, though there is currently no consensus regarding his asking price. Furthermore, Inácio is left-footed and has primarily played as an outside centre-back throughout his career.

What the Rossoneri need right now is more of a right-footed player capable of rotating between a wide centre-back role and a central position. While it is true that Gonçalo adapted to the right side under Amorim, there are other candidates who are a more natural fit for that role.

For instance, Ismaelo Ganiou of RC Lens has been on the radar for some time. His contract renewal in August does not necessarily rule out a transfer, although there has been no further contact with the French club since initial discussions in the summer.

Among the new names, 21-year-old Massiré Sylla of Union Saint-Gilloise is an intriguing prospect. The Belgian club have also moved quickly to secure their young star with a new contract until 2031. That said, it is not a major obstacle, and the price is around €15m.

#1724. Are you ok, Noni?

Arsenal’s squad construction has given them a lot of depth and diversity in terms of profiles. Timber and White for right-back, Calafiori and Hincapie for left-back. Ezri Konsa has, incredibly, offered both protection and threat to the impregnable Saliba and Gabriel partnership. Bruno and Lewis Skelly, Rice and Zubimendi and Odegaard and Merino for midfield.

Eze and Tzolis for the left-wing. Havertz and Gyokeres for centre-forward. Of course, some of these pairings are more symbiotic than others. Mosquera is probably going to fall behind Konsa as a back up to either one of Saliba or Gabriel. In reality, Zubimendi is only going to play ahead of Rice if Rice is injured or Arsenal have a nice easy game against League Two opposition, for example…

On the face of it, Noni Madueke should really be in that third layer of the squad with Mosquera, Kepa and where Zubimendi probably now resides. The role of back-up to Bukayo Saka ought to have been one with limited opportunity. In a sense, I was always a little surprised that Madueke signed up for it when he came to the club from Chelsea last summer.

I was slightly surprised that Arsenal spent so much money on a player who was always incredibly unlikely to dislodge Saka no matter how much he improved. And how much scope was there going to be for Madueke to get the sort of rhythm and consistency of selection to hone his talents?

Now I strongly suspect that Arsenal would have had anxieties over Saka’s ability to stay fit after tearing his hamstring in December 2024 and missing a few months of football. It was the first significant injury Saka had incurred and after quickly deciding that loanee winger Raheem Sterling was not going to be an adequate replacement, they amended for his absence with a blend of 17-year-old Ethan Nwaneri and surplus left-back Kieran Tierney.

It isn’t difficult to see how Arsenal viewed the right-wing spot as a single point of failure but encouraging Madueke to see it as an attractive position must have challenged even Mikel Arteta’s powers of persuasion. Yet just over a year on from signing for Arsenal, Madueke has a league title winners medal (‘while others are tweeting and posting’) with 25 starts to his name last season, 16 of which were in the Premier League.

In reality, being Bukayo Saka’s third leg has, to this point, proved to be a savvy career move for Madueke because he is getting plenty of time on the pitch in Saka’s increasing absences. This extends to the England National Team too, where Madueke plays the same role. But it was a role that still earned him four starts for his country in a World Cup, including a start in the quarter-final against Norway.

A Premier League title winners medal, a Champions League Final appearance and four World Cup starts was not a bad return for Madueke in terms of playing time. I think we knew when Arsenal bought him that Noni was a talented but phlegmatic player, relentless in taking on his full-back but the quality of his end-product could vary markedly.

In his new signing profile of Madueke on Arseblog, Phil Costa wrote, ‘there’s a feeling that Arsenal lack penetration from their wingers (Bukayo Saka aside); chaos factor, some unpredictability, and Madueke brings this in spades. His first thought when receiving the ball is centred around provoking defenders and driving towards goal, which means you can isolate him without too much focus on the overall setup – you just wind him up and let him go.

‘There are two specific metrics to love when assessing the 23-year-old; per FBRef data, he currently sits in the 95th percentile for progressive carries (6.82 per 90) and the 98th percentile for carries into the box (4.12 per 90). Those are big numbers.’ There was never any doubt about Madueke’s ability to get the ball into threatening areas, the question has always been what he does when he gets there.

Last season, some clips of him harumphing the ball out of the stadium on his right foot went semi-viral. I also think some of his performances were impacted by a lack of balance in the front three. With technicians like Havertz and Odegaard unavailable, he was often playing alongside fellow blunderbusses like Gyokeres and Martinelli.

I admit that my tolerance for inefficiency is high when it comes to attackers. I think attacking is a volume game. The vast majority of attacks come to nothing, the vast majority of shots do not go in or even work a goalkeeper. Individual attacks are the weather but, overall, attacking is the climate. The more you do it and sustain it, the more likely you are to score.

So my ‘we can fix him’ gene for slightly wayward wingers is high. I didn’t even mind Gervinho (a frustrating player, no doubt, but the Bradford miss has become the defining image of his Arsenal career which I don’t believe was fully representative of his performances).

The video of Madueke’s right foot ballooning the ball into the upper tier against Kairat last season has been refined. Both his goals this season have been on his right foot, particularly notably against Nottingham Forest where he cut in on his right and unleashed a low and controlled shot. It might have taken a helpful deflection but that’s because he kept the attempt low.

Last season, his right footed efforts were more in danger of colliding with low flying aircraft on their way into orbit. Noni’s goal against Slavia Praha demonstrated his pace in behind. It was the sort of goal and chance Gabriel Martinelli was hoovering up in Europe last season. European games tend to offer more space in behind and with Martinelli gone, Madueke is one of the few Arsenal attackers explosive enough to exploit it.

Indeed, in my view, he ought to have won Arsenal a match winning penalty in Budapest against Paris Saint Germain in May. There are signs of greater maturity and efficiency in his game. According to WhoScored.com his pass success rate in the Premier League last season was 76.2%. This season so far it is 86.3%.

I think he has learned that he does not have to go for the full-back at 100mph every single time he gets the ball and has varied his game. In the Champions League game against Lille, he sent 15 crosses into the penalty area, having sent six into the area in the game before against Leeds. 15 crosses sounds like a lot but it was very clearly under instruction from Mikel Arteta.

After that Lille game, the manager said of Madueke, ‘I said when you talk about players being ‘clinical’, sometimes that means scoring five in every 100. It’s about generating volume, more actions and getting him into the good positions, because he will decide matches. He had a really big contribution a few days ago, today he had a contribution in the last final pass as well.’

Being omitted from the England squad in September, according to Arteta, provided additional motivation for Noni, ‘After the break, he is showing something else, another level of anger, another level of conviction as well as in his actions and he is becoming decisive in matches, which is what we expect from a player like him.’

He has now been omitted from the England squad again for the November international round. It is a decision I don’t really understand from Thomas Tuchel but I am happy if it continues to provide Madueke with an additional reason to fine tune his game and because it hopefully protects a player who has become very important.

I admit I am not entirely sure how good Madueke is going to be in, say, three years’ time. He is 24 and it’s at that age that attackers typically start to increase their decisive actions. He has Max Dowman in the rearview mirror too. I think Madueke has a really high ceiling and there are small, but encouraging, signs of improvement.

#1723. Attacking efficiency key for Hull’s visit

Arsenal are in Premier League action this afternoon, taking on Hull City at home. No doubt there will be some rotation from the midweek Champions League game, with players like Martin Odegaard, Bruno Guimaraes, Myles-Lewis-Skelly, Jurrien Timber, Riccardo Calafiori, Christos Tzolis and Kai Havertz all potential inclusions. I suspect Declan Rice will start!

I wrote yesterday about Viktor Gyokeres and whether his good performance in midweek would see him keep his place. On the Swedish international, Mikel Arteta said:

I think everybody was so happy to see, not only the goals but also the performance, how free he looked, how happy he looked, the energy that he could transmit on that football pitch. That’s exactly what we need, that’s what we’re signing, that’s the type of player that can help us to make the difference and he certainly did that during the night.

So let’s see if that means he keeps his place up front. Noni Madueke has had a decent couple of weeks too, with the manager revealing he’d used the elongated Interlull in October to up the ante in terms of his own training:

What he did is he went abroad and he trained. He got somebody to train him and he went into a programme, he wanted to do that. That’s Noni and that’s his mindset – he wants to get better. I love that action that he took because at that moment he wasn’t playing.

With Bukayo Saka injured and Max Dowman suspended until after the Newcastle game, he’s more or less the only option on the right-hand side, so fingers crossed he can continue that form today against a team who are likely to try and make life difficult for us. Players who can beat a man and find some space are really valuable for fixtures like this, and he might prove very important later on.

Hull started the season brightly, but haven’t won since the end of August. All the same, five draws from their last seven games tells you they’re a relatively tough nut to crack, and with a back five they’ll surely have looked at how other teams have come to our place to frustrate us. An early goal is always useful, Ezri Konsa’s quick strike against Everton probably prevented that game from being as much of a slog as it might have been, but we might also need some patience today too.

Some of the difficult games they’ve come through and competed in, they’ve earned the right to be here and been impressive. We’ve been discussing that with the boys on what to expect from them tomorrow and to be clear on what we need to do to beat them.

Arsenal were a bit wasteful in midweek against Slavia Prague, and so making the most of our chances will be important today. Whether it’s Gyokeres or Havertz, and regardless of the construction of the midfield, we need to be more clinical as a team in general, so let’s hope we can produce that today. I take nothing for granted in this league, but hopefully this is one we can just deal with as efficiently as possible before we head into the Interlull.

I just want to mention the launch of The 22 we had at Big Red last night, a huge thanks to everyone who came along and bought a book. The reaction to it was fantastic, and it was real pleasure to meet so many of you. A massive thanks too to Martin and Louise and all the staff there who were such a great help – with the Tollington closed for a while, Big Red is open today if you’re looking for your pre-game pints.

The last batch of books will go on general sale today at 6pm (UK time) via this link (which will be live at that time): https://www.yumastudios.com/store/p/the-22

Orders are limited to two per person, and once they sell out, that’s it. This is a real collector’s item, and the best of luck if you’re after one.

Right, I’ll leave it there for this morning. As ever, we’ll bring you live blog coverage of the game later, as well all the post-game stuff on Arseblog News like the match report, player ratings, manager reaction, quotes round-up and more. There’s also a preview podcast on Patreon if you need something to listen to ahead of kick off. Don’t forget the updated Arseblog apps also have a cool new matchday centre, full of stats, alerts, and much more.

Hopefully catch some of you a bit later on!

#1722. Arsenal 1-0 Hull: Not efficient, but enough

In yesterday’s preview blog, I spoke about Arsenal’s attacking efficiency, and how that might be key to taking all three points. In yesterday’s game against Hull, Arsenal took 21 shots, 10 of which were on target, and scored one goal from that. Efficient?

Despite generally dominating possession, I thought there was a lack of precision in certain aspects of our first half play. Passes weren’t quite quick enough or accurate enough, but there were moments when we could have found the breakthrough. Gabriel almost got on the end of a Noni Madueke cross which was flicked on towards the back post, Rice had a tame shot from a free kick before a late header which he probably should have done better with.

And then there was Kai Havertz. It’s fair to say Hull didn’t leave a lot of room behind a defensive line that often had six players stretched across it, but late in the half a superb Martin Odegaard pass sent him clean through, one on one with the keeper. I haven’t seen replays but in real time I felt like he should have pulled the trigger – instead he over-complicated it. You have to be prepared to shoot from there, even if it’s on your wrong foot.

Then there was a penalty incident when he complained vociferously, play went on, the ref was then told to go to the screen and we all assumed it would be a penalty. However, the ref said it was a foul but Havertz was offside – and it felt like a massive waste of time. Afterwards, it emerged it should have been a penalty, but apparently the rule is ‘open to interpretation’. So clear as mud then.

In the second half, we seemed to play down our right a lot, with Madueke the outlet most of the time. I thought he did pretty well, much better than Christos Tzolis on the other side, but the breakthrough wouldn’t come. Mikel Merino replaced Rice (who seemed to be on the end of a wild challenge in midfield that the ref just ignored as he tumbled through the air), and Viktor Gyokeres came on for Havertz.

On 71 minutes though, we found the goal. Madueke’s shot was spilled by the keeper, Odegaard was quickest to react to poke the ball home for 1-0. And to be fair, you always felt confident that would be enough. We are the masters of the single goal margin win, and this was another one. Not a day that will live long in the memory or anything, but a 1-0 win that takes us into the Interlull in really good shape, and there’s not much arguing with that.

Or really, much more to say about this game. Mikel Arteta sounded happy enough, saying:

I’m delighted with the win. To go into the international break with a win is one of the best things about being a coach or player, I would say. Regarding the performance, I thought we were the better team, had enough chances to score and make it bigger for ourselves and we weren’t efficient enough to take them.

We then had to rely on generating volume, plenty of persisting until we finally broke them down. Martin then got the goal. Not the most beautiful one, but the most effective one, a simple ‘shoot and then follow the next action’, and that was ultimately enough to win the game.

So Arsenal sit top of the table, with 9 wins from 10 so far this season in the league, and it’s a very impressive run of form. Do I wish we had more attacking potency? Absolutely, and I do worry a bit that it might bite us in the arse somewhere down the line, but for now, we can see that this is a team that just knows how to win, and perhaps that’s the most important thing.

Right, I’m gonna leave it there for this morning. I have to head back to Dublin today. It was great to see lots of you over the weekend, until next time! And we’ll have an Arsecast Extra for you tomorrow too.

#1721. PSG news: Three contract extensions close as talks begin with another key player

By Axel Clody | 13 Nov 2026 07:27

Paris Saint-Germain are working on contract extensions within their squad and making good progress. Three deals are well advanced, while a new one has just been launched.

As last year at the same time, PSG have embarked on a contract extension operation. Le Parisien has just provided an update on the files launched by the capital club and their progress. It emerges that the extensions of Ousmane Dembele and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia are well advanced.

The extension of the 2025 Ballon d’Or winner has been expected for many months and should indeed happen. He will be tied to the capital club until June 2030. The Georgian winger should also follow suit and commit until June 2032.

Negotiations are well under way between the two parties, while the two-time European champions have not wanted to change the terms of the extension, despite the serious knee injury suffered by the former Napoli man. Paris support their player and still want to count on him in the long term.

As previously reported, PSG want to extend two academy graduates: Quentin Ndjantou and David Boly. According to Le Parisien, negotiations are advanced to extend the contract of the former. The 19-year-old, who can play as a left winger or in midfield, should be tied to the capital club until June 2031.

Alongside these well-advanced and almost concluded files, there are others whose outcome is not imminent.

Paris also intend to keep David Boly and are working on the signing of his first professional contract. The 17-year-old right-back, who also wants to remain at his boyhood club, is Eintracht Frankfurt’s priority and is also wanted by Arsenal.

Discussions are therefore under way between the two parties, as they are between the Paris hierarchy and Desire Doue. Talks began several weeks ago but are not yet very advanced. This file should take time, but that does not mean the trend is negative.

Le Parisien also reveals that PSG are considering extending the face of the club: Marquinhos. The Brazilian defender joined the capital club in 2013 and has become a legend and Luis Enrique’s current captain. The 32-year-old is getting older but is still performing as well as ever.

The Paris hierarchy has therefore raised the possibility of a new contract with Marquinhos’ entourage, with his deal expiring in 2028. The position of the former Roma player is not yet known.

#1720. Cherki magic helping Maresca to step out of Guardiola shadow

Rumours of Manchester City’s supposed demise without Pep Guardiola appear to be much exaggerated.

They swept past Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park with a style of play under new manager Enzo Maresca that was just as swashbuckling as under his predecessor, with Rayan Cherki playing the role of chief architect. The Frenchman’s two goals included a captivating mazy dribble, which will long be remembered by those who had the fortune to see it.

City created enough space for themselves through clever movement. With Cherki zigging one way and Phil Foden zagging the other, they created even more by dribbling past a mesmerised Palace back three that became a back five at times and still could not cope.

Erling Haaland also scored twice. Even with the creative and unpredictable talents of those behind in a four-man attacking City midfield, Haaland remains irreplaceable with his ability to convert chances.

However, this night belonged to Cherki. Guardiola chided him publicly after he set up a City goal with a “rabona” cross last season. The thrust of Guardiola’s comments were that Cherki was not Lionel Messi. Of course not, but he possesses a genius all of his own, which Maresca would surely be foolish to rein in.

The jaw-dropping splendour of Cherki’s first goal drew a collective intake of breath at Selhurst Park.

Collecting a Foden pass, he attacked the Palace area on a diagonal path, slaloming between Jaydee Canvot, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chris Richards, before having the spatial awareness and technique to flick his left foot at the ball to send it rolling on a perpendicular trajectory past Dean Henderson.

"The man with the magic feet!"Rayan Cherki doubles Manchester City's lead with a STUNNING goal 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/9Zea5vFljv

An insight into Cherki’s mindset came after the match.

He said: “My performance is s---. In the first half, we didn’t find the space, I played bad. I need to show them that I want to play, I want to score. Next time I want to give the ball around more.”

Forget the words, Maresca cannot ignore the actions of a player he left on the bench against Bournemouth.

Sterner tests will come for City than against a Palace side missing key players who may or may not leave south London in the remaining days of the transfer window.

Whether Maresca will trust his forward players to express themselves as freely against their rivals for the Premier League title remains to be seen, but with Elliot Anderson providing a one-man shield behind them, City could not be stopped.

Maresca said: “For sure Rayan is happy tonight. His performance was very good and not just for his two goals. He has to press off the ball and he was in charge of [marking] Adam Wharton, so it was a complete game by him.”

Only for the first three minutes did Palace hint at a different outcome but, after shots from Eddie Nketiah and Daichi Kamada were diverted away for corners, City took control.

They took the lead in the 17th minute when the otherwise quiet Antoine Semenyo flighted a cross over the heads of everyone except the shorn locks of Haaland, whose determined header looped over Henderson and dropped in the far corner.

The only negative of Foden’s performance came in front of goal, with a ballooned shot and a mistimed header.

After Cherki’s solo masterpiece had made it 2-0, Yeremy Pino seized the next moment for his own with a stunning free-kick that flicked the crossbar, then the back of City keeper Gianluigi Donnarumma before finally dropping over the line.

"This is a good a free-kick as you're likely to see this season!" Yéremy Pino's stirke beats Donnarumma 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5uF4vzOXDp

Whatever hope that mustered was snatched away again when Cherki scored his second goal and the third goal of a breathless five minutes.

His shot at the end of a darting run flicked the ankle of Tomiyasu to send it just out of Henderson’s reach.

Rayan Cherki AGAIN! Manchester City have breathing room once again after another strike from the Frenchman 👏 pic.twitter.com/Tyw9whPS2r

Morocco teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi had little time to show why City have paid Lille £85.6m for him with a late entry as a substitute, but they didn’t need him on this occasion.

Foden then set off on a swerving run that set up Haaland to lash home his second goal of the game and make it 4-1.

Erling Haaland scores gets another! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/4mz2eF7wFF

The fear for Palace is that they cannot keep selling their best players and expecting to replicate the success on the pitch that has brought them three trophies in the past 15 months.

Leicester City offer a shuddering example of that. From Premier League champions to League One in 10 seasons.

Pierre Sage, the new Palace manager, will welcome the certainty that the closure of the transfer window will bring, particularly over the futures of forwards Ismaïla Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta, as well as wing-back Daniel Muñoz.

The one player he cannot afford to lose is Wharton, who matched the City midfield on his own at times in the first half.

Sage said: “I think the score is heavy. We stayed in the game for 65 minutes and created some chances. We know we are in for a tough season, but we have created a lot of opportunities in the first two games.

“I could speak about the transfer window, but I don’t want to find an excuse. We just have to be sure that in four days’ time, the team will be better than today.”

“It has been a short pre-season. Rayan [Cherki], five weeks ago was at the World Cup. Game by game, we will be back, just need a few games. We played well, it is a new manager but we have been playing together, with the addition of a few new players. We know what to do and have to trust the system.”

“We have to keep on playing together, find out where we are best and how to play. We have so many good players and we have to fit everyone in. He has to keep going because we know how good Phil is, it is about showing it week in week out. This is the right step forward for everyone. We have to build on this.”

"I'm just trying to play my football" 💪Elliot Anderson is excited about the future at Manchester City after his summer transfer 🔥 pic.twitter.com/huGv4Li3GZ

"Say what you actually mean!" 🤣Erling Haaland takes over Rayan Cherki's post-match interview! pic.twitter.com/adW6IU8DzQ

2 + 2 - Rayan Cherki is the third player to have a game with multiple goals and another game with multiple assists across a team's first two matches of a Premier League campaign, after Thierry Henry in 2004-05 and Didier Drogba in 2010-11.Polymath. pic.twitter.com/4cRV0xMIFa

September 5: Fulham vs Crystal PalaceSeptember 12: Crystal Palace vs IpswichSeptember 19: Leeds vs Crystal PalaceOctober 11: Crystal Palace vs Nottingham ForestOctober 18: Brighton vs Crystal Palace

Pierre Sage’s side will host Middlesbrough in the League Cup third round next month and will also begin their Europa League campaign in September.

The directions of these teams will be diverging this season. City were wonderful, free-flowing, expressive and fun to watch. Palace not so much. It will take Pierre Sage a while to impose his style of play. It will certainly take another week before he knows his final squad for the first half of the season.

It was noticeable at the final whistle that many Palace fans stayed around to applaud Daniel Munoz, an unused substitute on the night, as he made his way to the tunnel, probably for the final time as a Palace player if Nottingham Forest’s interest in him becomes a transfer by the end of the window.

"Cherki was the difference" 🪄"He is a genius" 🧠Jamie Redknapp reacts to Crystal Palace 1-4 Man City 🔊 pic.twitter.com/UjSarMngDR

Pretty comprehensive in Manchester City’s favour, which is reflected in the scoreline.

The final whistle is blown at Selhurst Park and Manchester City have cruised to a 4-1 win thanks to doubles from Cherki and Haaland. Enzo Maresca’s side make it two wins from two whereas it is two defeats from two for Pierre Sage.

Manchester City, with the three points already in the bag, are just stroking the ball around with ease and are in complete control. Palace can barely get a foot on it.

A late double substitution for Manchester City as Reis and Braithwaite come on. Enzo Maresca’s side are cruising to victory to make it two wins from two.

Cherki has two goals to his name and now Haaland does as Manchester City are romping to victory in south London. There is going to be a debut for the Premier League’s most expensive teenager ever as Bouaddi comes on for Manchester City. McAidoo is also coming on, with Cherki and Anderson going off.

Mingueza eventually comes on but not after having to wait until the ball goes out of play again as Khalaili was adjudged to have taken too long to have got off the pitch. That change does mean that Palace have used all five substitutions, which means Munoz will not come on. Crystal Palace make another double change and it will be two debuts as Disasi and Mingueza come on.

Enzo Maresca turns to his bench for the first time tonight as Kovacic comes on.

Palace are going to make a double substitution as McNeil and Gozo replace Nketiah and Pino. 19-year-old Gozo is on for his Palace debut.

That was a chance for Palace. Guessand finds Pino, who drives into the Manchester City penalty area on the right. Pino has Nketiah at the far post but there is too much on the cross.

Guessand, back at Palace, is going to come on to replace Strand Larsen, who has been pretty quiet up top for the home side tonight.

Sometimes you feel blessed to witness an extraordinary moment of footballing genius. Selhurst Park has just seen two in the space of three minutes. Yeremy Pino’s free-kick which flicked off the back of Gianluigi Donnarumma was stunning, but even that could not truly compare to the slalom run of Rayan Cherki that drew a collective intake of breath from all those present. The Frenchman has just followed it with a scorching shot. It couldn’t compare with his first, though.

Three goals come in quick succession and Cherki restores Manchester City’s two-goal advantage with his second of the night. The Frenchman receives it on the turn from around 30 yards out and drives towards the Palace penalty area. He then shoots and a kind deflection off Richards takes it over Henderson’s diving effort and into the Palace net.

Rayan Cherki AGAIN! Manchester City have breathing room once again after another strike from the Frenchman 👏 pic.twitter.com/Tyw9whPS2r

Just as the hosts appeared to maybe out of this one, they get a goal back. Pino’s fantastic free-kick strikes the bar, hits Donnarumma on the back before going into the net off the post. That hit the frame of the goal twice and Palace have a crucial goal, minutes after going 2-0 down.

"This is a good a free-kick as you're likely to see this season!" Yéremy Pino's stirke beats Donnarumma 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5uF4vzOXDp

Anderson brings down Pino not far outside the Manchester City penalty area and is booked.

The next goal in this game felt crucial and the visitors have it. Foden drives towards the Palace penalty area before playing a pass forward into the path of Cherki. "The man with the magic feet!"Rayan Cherki doubles Manchester City's lead with a STUNNING goal 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/9Zea5vFljv

No-one has had fewer touches on the pitch tonight than Haaland up until this point but the Norwegian’s goal is the difference. His number of touches (14) is the joint fewest with his compatriot Strand Larsen.

That was a good chance for Nketiah. He plays the ball to the underlapping Mitchell, who from the byline cuts it back into the path of Nketiah. The former Arsenal man should so so much better with his opportunity from the edge of the six-yard box but fires a long way wide.

Semenyo wins Manchester City an early corner in this second half off Canvot. Anderson’s delivery beyond the back post picks out O’Reilly, who in space heads back across goal but Pino heads away.

We are back under way at Selhurst Park, with Manchester City carrying a 1-0 lead into this second half. As the players emerged from the tunnels for the second half, the DJ at Selhurst Park paid tribute to the late Dolly Parton and Kenny Rogers by playing Islands in the Stream. Nice touch! Get your favourite Dolly and Kenny tunes in the comments section at the bottom of the blog.

The first half at Selhurst Park is then brought to an end and Manchester City lead 1-0 at the break thanks to Haaland’s header.

There will be just one added minute at the end of this first half.

Palace started off with a nominal back three. That has become a back five far too often for Pierre Sage’s liking at times in this first half, yet still City are playing through them almost at will. The Palace fans whose deafening support accompanied Palace shots in the opening minutes are reduced to cheering battling midfield runs that win a free-kick now.

Pino delivers a free-kick into the Manchester City box and Richards gets to it first. It comes off his shoulder and rolls into the arms of Donnarumma.

Palace now miss a big opportunity and should be on level terms. Wharton, who has probably been the best player on the pitch tonight, whips in a cross from the right and picks out Mitchell, who has a free header from eight yards out but somehow misses the target.

Strand Larsen comes close with a header from a Pino cross but he would have been offside anyway.

The first booking of the night goes the way of the visitors. Wharton drives forward into the Manchester City half and is cynically brought down by Cherki, who looked perplexed when the yellow card was shown but it was an obvious booking.

Foden wastes his second big chance of this first half. Manchester City break through O’Reilly, who carries it down the right. He waits for Cherki to make the overlapping run before passing to the Frenchman. Cherki’s cross picks out Foden inside the six-yard box and the latter should score but he gets a simple header all wrong.

Well, that was easy. So easy in fact – perfect Semenyo cross, perfect Haaland header - that it hushed Selhurst Park as the ball looped over Dean Henderson. Even the roar from the enclave of City fans took a moment to fill the south London air. You wouldn’t say that all the pre-match optimism among Palace fans has been punctured, but the home side need a moment if they aren’t to sink without trace to a City side bossing possession and territory now.

That is a huge miss from Foden. Anderson picks out his compatriot in acres of space on the right side of the box, with no Palace defender within five yards of him, but Foden blazes over the bar when he should have put Manchester City 2-0 up.

King Harald V of Norway has died in the last few days and over the last few hours two Norwegian cyclists claimed a one-two at the Vuelta a Espana and now Haaland has a goal.

He has barely touched the ball thus far but he puts the visitors ahead just past the quarter-of-an-hour mark. Semenyo is afforded too much space on the left just outside the penalty area and clips in a cross towards the far post. Haaland gets up highest, above Richards, and guides a superb header over Henderson into the Palace net.

Erling Haaland gets off the mark for the new Premier League season! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/5ZjQUVk6Zl

The England boss is in attendance tonight, perhaps keeping a close eye on that midfield battle between Anderson and Wharton.

Palace flirt with danger inside their own penalty area. After Haaland’s flick, Kamada should just belt the ball away but instead inexplicably leaves it. Henderson manages to mop up just as Foden was eyeing up the chance.

Quite a lot of the focus tonight will be on two English midfielders; one who has got a big-money move this summer and the other thus far has not. Anderson is directly up against Wharton and so far it is the latter who is winning the early battles, including dispossessing Anderson in midfield.

The first chance of the game goes the way of the hosts. It stems from a quite sensational first-time pass from Wharton from inside his own half into the left channel to pick out the run of Nketiah, whose shot from the left side of the box takes a deflection off Dias and is saved by Donnarumma.

Manchester City initially clear the corner but Palace keep it alive. Kamada’s shot from just inside the box appeared to be on target but it is headed over for another corner, which is easily caught by Donnarumma.

We are under way at Selhurst Park. Will Pierre Sage earn his first win as Palace boss or can Enzo Maresca and City make it two wins from two?

Both sides emerge from the tunnel in the corner of Selhurst Park to the customary sound of Glad All Over and we are moments away from kick-off in south London. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

It isn’t a simple task to attract an opposition player’s attention when you are leaning over a barrier a few feet higher than him – and in the home end. Haaland and his teammates have the look of a team that knows it must perform tonight to ease the concerns that they are a team in transition. The City fans will not entertain such thoughts, either.

Crystal Palace looked set to sign Club Brugge defender Joel Ordonez but that deal could be in doubt as there may be some problems with his medical. We await to see further updates on that situation.

Both Ismaila Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta are out of the Crystal Palace squad tonight with injury but could they be on the move before the window slams shut? Sarr has been linked with Galatasaray and Liverpool whilst the situation is complicated with Mateta as he claims the final year of his contract is void. How do those two situations resolve themselves? Daniel Munoz has been linked with a move to Nottingham Forest but is on the bench for Palace this evening.

An unfulfilled wish so far for a young Palace fan holding up a child’s red Norway shirt with ‘Haaland’ emblazoned on it. Having waited patiently for the City players to emerge for their warm-up and being held by his dad as he leant over the stone wall to attract Haaland’s attention, he was left disappointed because the City striker was simply not looking as he and his teammates jogged past. Was it really just a year ago when Crystal Palace fans flooded down the Holmesdale Road with not a care in the world having just won the Community Shield to add to their FA Cup triumph over tonight’s opponents Manchester City? Well, they are marching along the Holmesdale Road in the same numbers again this evening, bedecked in red and blue as always, yet there is uncertainty and worry in the air and on their faces. Will the player exodus continue? What should they make of new manager Pierre Sage? Will the good times fade from view as quickly as they did for Leicester City or can Sage build a new side to match the one which, under Oliver Glasner, added the Conference League to their list of trophies three months ago?

“We struggled to get into the game and win the battles,” a disappointed Carlo Ancelotti lamented.

At the World Cup, an industrious 18-year-old showed maturity beyond his years to dominate the midfield against Ancelotti’s Brazil on his competitive international debut, earning Morocco a draw. That was, in fact, the second time an Ancelotti side had been undone by precocious teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Ancelotti’s remarks about losing the midfield battle are from after a Champions League match in October 2024, when Lille shocked Real Madrid to end their 36-game unbeaten run. Bouaddi was at the heart of both statement results for his club and country.

The second weekend of the Premier League season kicks off under the lights in South London as Crystal Palace host Manchester City at Selhurst Park. Manchester City won both fixtures 3-0 last season and they are in fact unbeaten in their last 11 Premier league away games against Crystal Palace, who have won just two of the 22 top flight meetings.

Crystal Palace experienced defeat on the opening weekend, falling to a 2-0 loss at Everton last Saturday, meaning the Pierre Sage era started with a defeat. Tonight is Sage’s first home game in charge of the club.

“I think it will be a wonderful moment, but I prefer to have a wonderful moment with good news at the end of the game,” Sage said. “That is why I do not think about me in this situation. The most important thing is the team and the result for sure, because we prepare all the week for that, to make them [the fans] happy. They will be happy to see us, but I think they would prefer to see us win. I will give my life to make them happy. I cannot do more. When you are in this stadium [Selhurst Park], you feel the history. You feel that there is something heavy weighing on you. It is a great responsibility that I have been entrusted with. We cannot wait to see this stadium in action.”

Sage has confirmed that Ismaila Sarr, who has been linked with a move away from the club this summer, and Chadi Riad will miss out tonight due to injury, as will striker Jean-Philippe Mateta. Palace have confirmed the addition of Axel Disasi on loan from Chelsea and the French defender could be involved tonight.

Manchester City appeared to be heading towards defeat in Enzo Maresca’s first league game in charge of the club last weekend. They were 1-0 down at home against Bournemouth in the closing stages before goals from Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol gave them a come-from-behind win.

It has been a busy week in the transfer window for Manchester City. Both Savio (formerly Savinho) and Omar Marmoush have left for Tottenham, joining a long list of departures from the Etihad this summer. Moroccan midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi has arrived in an £85m deal from Lille and has become the most expensive teenager in Premier League history. Maresca has confirmed that 18-year-old Bouaddi is ready to start.

“He [Bouaddi] is ready,” Maresca said. “He was working with his former club so he is fit. We will see how long he needs in terms of adaptation but he is ready to go. He is quite calm. He does not look 18, he already looks older, which is important. But in this case, we need to go slowly because he is very young, he has come from a different country so there is no rush for him. He is going to help us now and in the future. He is very mature for being 18.”

Team news from Selhurst Park to follow shortly.

#1719. Strops, scruff, and chaos

I watched Man Utd v Aston Villa last night. When Villa conceded late on to let a two goal lead slip for the second time in the game, Unai Emery threw a strop and went down the tunnel. It’s not the first time he’s eschewed a handshake with the opposition manager, and his post-game interview where he insisted he thought the game was over was very funny because it was such obvious bullshit.

This is someone who has managed over 1000 games in his career. I’m pretty sure he knows when the final whistle blows and when it doesn’t. Can you imagine if Mikel Arteta did that? You wouldn’t be able to move for all the opinion pieces about what a sore loser he is and all the rest. But perhaps Emery gets a pass because he is ‘the best manager in the league’. Anyway, perhaps it provides a stay of execution for Michael Carrick at Man Utd, which can only be a good thing.

Meanwhile, it looks as if Pierre Sage is gonna get fired by Crystal Palace and replaced by Thomas Frank. That seems a sensible appointment to me. Enough time has passed since his spell at Sp*rs for the toxins to wear off, and he’s clearly a good manager. I’ve never been convinced by Sage, I just think he looks too scruffy. As if someone got a 10 year old to draw man and brought it to life.

I quite enjoyed this quote from Mikel Arteta in his post-game press conference after Saturday’s 1-0 win over Hull:

Sometimes we try to score the perfect goal against low blocks, but we need to be much more chaotic than that. If we open the scoring much earlier also, it changes the game.

I love it as a concept, adding some chaos to our control makes a lot of sense, but it also kinda seems at odds with what the manager asks of his players. Maybe he just means more shots from distance, maybe riskier pass when we’re trying to break the opposition down, or maybe there’s something he’s got cooking for over the Interlull and when we return we see something we never expected. He did kick the shit out of a dugout chair on Saturday, that’s a new enough development to be fair.

I wonder was he referring to the Kai Havertz chance in the first half, when he could have shot on his right foot but tried to cut back/lay it off. If you shoot, maybe you don’t score but as we saw with the winning goal from Martin Odegaard, it might end up in the path of another Arsenal player who can finish it off. Perhaps too there’s a bit of a through line between being more chaotic and what Noni Madueke is doing at the moment. He can be a bit scattergun, but as Nick Wright points out on Sky Sports, his numbers are improving. I don’t think Arteta will ever embrace full chaos, all the time, but if he can add a little more to the mix, it could certainly help.

Right, I have to leave it there for this morning. A bit shorter than normal, I know. We will have an Arsecast Extra for you a bit later on though. We’ve already put out the call for questions on BlueSky @gunnerblog.bsky.social and @arseblog.com, so fire away using the hashtag #arsecastextra – or if you’re an Arseblog Member on Patreon, leave your question in the #arsecast-extra-questions channel on our Discord server.

The pod should be out around around lunchtime. Until then, have a good one.

#1718. Tuttosport: Milan rekindle interest in Bologna star amid feeling of regret

AC Milan still retain an interest in signing Juan Miranda after being linked with him in previous years, a report claims.

Tuttosport write this morning that Miranda is establishing himself as one of the best specialists in his position in Europe. The numbers speak for themselves: he’s already provided six assists in the first part of the season.

No one in Serie A has more than that, and his creativity was seen first hand in Bologna’s comeback win at San Siro. Naturally, his performances have not gone unnoticed in Italy and England. The first inquiries are beginning to arrive, with a contract situation that is worth keeping an eye on.

The paper writes that Miranda is also appreciated by Milan, although the Rossoneri are kicking themselves a bit too. They had an agreement to sign him on a free transfer two years ago and then decided to walk away. In hindsight, it looks like a big mistake.

Bologna seized the transfer opportunity in the summer of 2024, and are now enjoying his exploits. At the same time, however, concern is beginning to mount given that his deal with the Rossoblu expires in just 19 months.

This is why the Bologna management have been trying to establish talks regarding a contract extension in the past few weeks. The work so far hasn’t led to great progress, and so the possibility of a sale to avoid losing the Spaniard in a cut-price deal (or even for free) may be evaluated.

Juventus are in the running too, and an immediate attempt to bring him to Continassa and give Luciano Spalletti the left-back he’s coveted since last summer can’t be ruled out. This is especially true if the Bianconeri are in contention for a top-four finish.

Beware of the Palladino effect: since the coach took over at Bologna, the Rossoblu have been soaring (17 points in seven games). If the Emilian side were to also be involved in the fight for a European spot, it would be more difficult to pry Miranda from them.
